papers.title: Epitope-guided optimization improves the protective efficacy of NA-based mRNA vaccines against seasonal influenza A(H3N2) virus.
papers.authors: Kim H, Lee S, Cho S, Shin W, Lee S, Demirev AV, Lee T, Kim YJ, Kim D, Song SA, Jun KR, Kim JI.
papers.abstract: Neuraminidase (NA) is increasingly recognized as a promising target antigen for improving the breadth and durability of influenza vaccines, yet NA-based mRNA vaccines remain comparatively unexplored relative to hemagglutinin-based approaches. Here, we applied a computationally guided NA antigen-design strategy to seasonal H3N2 influenza viruses and investigated whether epitope-guided optimization could improve the immunogenicity and protective efficacy of NA-based mRNA vaccines. NA-D3, an NA antigen designed based on the evolutionary characteristics of circulating H3N2 viruses, was first evaluated in an mRNA vaccine. This vaccine provided partial protection against H3N2 challenge and reduced viral replication in the lungs, although detectable neuraminidase inhibition (NAI) activity was not observed. To further improve NA antigen immunogenicity, predicted B- and T-cell epitopes were incorporated into the antigen design process, resulting in three sequentially optimized NA candidates, F0, F1, and F2. In a subsequent challenge experiment, F1 and F2 conferred complete protection, achieving 100% survival and significantly lower viral RNA levels and infectious viral titers in the lungs compared to controls. The optimized NA mRNA vaccines also induced detectable NAI activity against heterologous H3N2 viruses, albeit at relatively modest levels. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the protective potential of NA-based mRNA vaccination against H3N2 influenza viruses and establish iterative, epitope-guided strategy in NA antigen optimization - integrating computational prediction with experimental validation - as an effective approach for developing broadly protective NA-based mRNA vaccines.

papers.title: Influenza H1N1 Imprinting Uncouples Serological and B-Cell Responses in Mice
papers.authors: Tjarnhage, E.; Le Quy, K.; Kasahara, T. d. M.; Daehli, M. L. T.; Greiff, V.; Grodeland, G.
papers.abstract: Antigenic drift reduces the protective potential of antibodies generated against earlier influenza variants. Unfortunately, a new infection or vaccination often preferentially recalls antibodies targeting previously encountered strains, thereby limiting responses to newly emerged variants. Although this phenomenon, known as immunological imprinting, has been well documented at the serological level, its underlying cellular mechanisms remain poorly understood. To resolve imprinting at both the serological and cellular level, we combined serum antibody profiling with targeted B-cell characterization in mice, including single-cell B-cell receptor (BCR) sequencing of germinal center (GC) B cells following secondary H1N1 challenge and bulk BCR sequencing of bone marrow plasma cells. We found that a primary infection with the 2009 pandemic H1N1 ("swine flu") strain largely prevented the generation of new serum antibodies following secondary exposure to the antigenically distinct H1N1 strain A/Puerto Rico/8/1934 (PR8), whereas the reciprocal infection sequence updated antibody specificities towards the last encountered virus. GC B cells did not mirror serological imprinting and instead generated updated BCR repertoires directed against the heterologous challenge strain. Likewise, BCR diversity in draining lymph node B cells failed to mirror the serological imprinting observed in the antibody response. Together, these findings reveal a striking uncoupling of cellular and serological immune responses during influenza imprinting, highlighting the need to study both compartments to better understand immune memory and guide the development of improved seasonal influenza vaccines across a diverse population.

papers.title: Digital twins forecast individual immune trajectories
papers.authors: Hu, C.; Yu, C.; Chen, C. Y.-C.
papers.abstract: The human immune system differs markedly between individuals and changes in response to infection, vaccination and treatment. AI virtual cells are being built to simulate cellular responses to perturbation. Yet these models, like most immune-response predictors, describe each person by a single pre-challenge measurement and forecast change from patterns pooled across people. Digital twins, updated with every new observation of an individual, could forecast how that person's immune state changes. Here we present ImmuneTwins, which builds these twins from single-cell profiles by personalizing a shared virtual-cell model with each individual's observations. In two external populations, ImmuneTwins reduced immune-age error by 32% and 42% relative to the best existing method. During repeated influenza vaccination, its twins predicted the direction of immune-cell change 35% more accurately than the best published method, and their error fell by 27% as observations accumulated. The twins revealed that immune cells and plasma proteins recover about half their deviation from a persistent personal reference within 90 days, whereas response size varies between challenges. They further localized B-cell remodelling in exceptional longevity and anticipated patient-specific immune trajectories during myeloma treatment. These results establish virtual-cell digital twins for forecasting individual immune change and identifying each person's characteristic immune features.

papers.title: Still's disease and malignancies: insights into the balance between inflammatory enhancement and immune control. Data from the International AIDA Network Still's Disease Registry.
papers.authors: Gavioli F, Sbalchiero J, Caggiano V, Hinojosa-Azaola A, Torres-Ruiz J, Martín-Nares E, Lopalco G, Morrone M, Del Vescovo S, Suzon B, Donat S, Giardini HAM, Ciccia F, Iacono D, Ruscitti P, Cipriani P, Almaghlouth IA, Sfriso P, Bindoli S, Kasapcopur O, Akay N, Konte EK, Batu ED, Ozen S, Bilginer Y, Ragab G, Mahmoud AAA, Sfikakis PP, Laskari K, Sota J, Tufan A, Erden A, Cakir IY, Emmi G, Fotis L, Kourtesi K, Karamanakos A, Dimouli A, Dagna L, Campochiaro C, Giacomelli R, Berardicurti O, Barone P, Papa S, Conti F, Gattamelata A, Thabet M, Frassi M, Crisafulli F, Direskeneli H, Alibaz-Oner F, Conforti A, Makowska J, Bugatti S, De Stefano L, Boyarchuk O, Pucino V, Govoni M, Rigante D, Al-Mayouf SM, Iagnocco A, Gicchino MF, Gaggiano C, Chimenti MS, Maiolini F, La Torre F, Hernández-Rodríguez J, Lo Gullo A, Moshrif A, Maggio MC, Conti G, Del Giudice E, Carubbi F, Guggino G, Ogunjimi B, Feist E, Balistreri A, Frediani B, Fabiani C, Cantarini L, Vitale A, From the International AIDA (AutoInflammatory Diseases Alliance) Network, from the Autoinflammatory Diseases Working Group of the Italian Society of Rheumatology (SIR).
papers.abstract: Still's disease is an autoinflammatory condition marked by excessive activation of the innate immune system, resulting in intense and persistent systemic inflammation if left untreated. Chronic inflammation is recognized as both an initiator and promoter of carcinogenesis, although growing evidence suggests it may act against cancer development. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the cancer risk in patients with Still's disease. Data were obtained from the international Autoinflammatory Diseases Alliance (AIDA) Network registry for Still's disease. Statistical analysis included a machine learning-based approach to evaluate associations between independent variables and malignancy. A total of 626 patients with Still's disease were included, of whom 14 (2.2%) developed 15 malignant neoplasms. Patients with malignancy history exhibited higher age at disease onset and diagnosis, as well as longer duration of fever during flares. Machine learning-based analysis, including Elastic Net and Firth's penalized likelihood logistic regression, identified an association between cancer development and fever duration (relative risk = 1.002, 95% confidence interval 1.000-1.004, p = 0.01). Despite being a severe systemic inflammatory condition, Still's disease appears to be associated with a relatively modest prevalence of cancer. However, uncontrolled systemic inflammation, as reflected by prolonged fever duration, may contribute to carcinogenesis in these patients.

papers.title: CD4 T cell surface architecture is associated with response to anti-PD-1 therapy in non-small cell lung cancer
papers.authors: Cinotti, R.; Yang, Y.; van Hoef, V.; van Ooijen, H.; Parling, A.; Geindreau, M.; Bigdeli, N.; Cruz de Los Santos, M.; Baldran-Groves, L.; Yang, Y.; Liu, L.; Johansson, M.; Karre, K.; Fredriksson, S.; de Petris, L.; Lundqvist, A.
papers.abstract: Anti-PD-1 therapy has substantially improved outcomes for patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but clinical responses remain highly heterogeneous and are difficult to predict. Current immune profiling approaches primarily characterize immune cell composition and protein abundance, whereas the spatial organization of proteins at the cell surface has remained largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate for the first time that cell surface protein organization is associated with clinical response to immune checkpoint inhibition therapy. Using the Proximity Network Assay (PNA), we simultaneously quantified cell frequencies, protein abundance, and protein organization in pretreatment peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 62 patients with advanced NSCLC treated with anti-PD-1 agents. While most cell populations were unchanged between responders and non-responders, pronounced response-associated alterations were identified within the CD4 T-cell compartment. Responders exhibited elevated expression of adhesion-associated proteins, and remodeling of a CD5-containing membrane domain. Increased colocalization within this domain was associated with poor clinical outcome and reduced survival. Machine learning analysis further identified CD4 T cell features as the strongest predictors of treatment response and demonstrated that protein organization provided greater predictive power than protein abundance alone. Together, these findings identify cell surface protein organization as a previously unexplored source of biomarkers and highlight its potential to improve immune profiling and biomarker discovery in cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts: origins, functional heterogeneity and therapeutic potential.
papers.authors: Zhou L, Tang M, Wang K, Wang N, Zhang J, Liu K, Li X, Dong Z.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are integral components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and are increasingly recognized as critical regulators of nearly every hallmark of cancer. Once viewed as a uniform, protumorigenic cell type, it is now clear that CAFs comprise a spectrum of dynamic and plastic functional states with both tumor-promoting and tumor-restraining capacities. This functional duality, conceptualized within the framework of cancer as a "wound that fails to heal", is dictated by their diverse cellular origins, the specific activation pathways engaged (such as TGF-β and PDGF), and the evolving cues from the TME. In this Review, we dissect the multifaceted roles of CAFs, from their promotion of cancer cell proliferation, invasion and angiogenesis through secreted factors and extensive extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, to their profound influence on the immune landscape. We detail how distinct CAF subsets, such as myofibroblastic (myCAFs) and inflammatory (iCAFs) CAFs, orchestrate an immunosuppressive niche and contribute to therapeutic resistance. We also explore the compelling evidence for tumor-suppressive CAF functions, which have catalyzed a paradigm shift in therapeutic strategies-moving away from indiscriminate CAF ablation towards nuanced approaches aimed at reprogramming their state. These strategies include modulating key signaling pathways, normalizing the CAF-remodeled ECM, and exploiting unique metabolic vulnerabilities. Finally, we discuss how advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are resolving this complexity, paving the way for the development of precision therapies that can selectively neutralize pro-tumorigenic CAF activities while harnessing their beneficial functions to improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: Inflammation reshapes epidermal and leukocyte differentiation resulting in altered glucocorticoid responsiveness
papers.authors: Faught, E.; Schrauwen, T.; Wijnants, A.; Escobar, N.; Kloet, S.; Meijer, A. H.; Schaaf, M.
papers.abstract: Glucocorticoids are widely prescribed anti-inflammatory drugs that act on nearly all cell types due to the ubiquitous expression of the glucocorticoid receptor (GR). While the molecular mechanisms of GR activation have been studied extensively, it is less well understood how GR signaling modulates cell type-specific responses during inflammation. Using the unique attributes of the zebrafish, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize GR-mediated transcriptional regulation under conditions of wounding-induced inflammation. We found specific cell populations that occurred only under inflammatory conditions within epidermal cells, macrophages and neutrophils. The inflammation-specific subset of epidermal cells showed elevated expression of inflammatory markers, and these cells exhibited a reduced transactivation response to dexamethasone. This reduction in GR activation was also observed in the inflammation-specific subset of macrophages, but not in neutrophils, which retained dexamethasone responsiveness. By correlating the dexamethasone responsiveness with transcriptional coregulator expression, we identified candidate regulatory mechanisms underlying differential GR responsiveness across cell types. Taken together, we provided unique mechanistic insights into cell differentiation during a local inflammatory response and cell type-specific glucocorticoid responsiveness in vivo.

papers.title: PANoptosis gene signatures identify candidate biomarkers and genetically associated genes in COPD.
papers.authors: Chen H, Wang J, Yang D, Ma T, Wang L, Wan Z, Zhu R.
papers.abstract: Background PANoptosis contributes to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) pathogenesis. We aimed to identify PANoptosis-related gene signatures as candidate biomarkers and evaluate their genetic associations with COPD risk. Methods Three transcriptomic data sets were integrated to identify differentially expressed PANoptosis-related genes in COPD, followed by enrichment analyses and immune infiltration profiling using CIBERSORT and single-sample gene set enrichment analysis. We selected feature genes using machine learning and evaluated their discriminative performance. We used Mendelian randomisation (MR) and multivariable MR (MVMR) to assess genetic associations with COPD risk, using the forced expiratory volume in one second/forced vital capacity (FEV1/FVC) ratio as a proxy for airflow limitation and adjusting for smoking. We validated candidate genes by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) in human lung tissues from COPD patients and controls. Results Seven PANoptosis-related genes (IL1B, IRF1, NTRK2, PIK3CG, SFN, TNFSF10, and UACA) were differentially expressed in COPD. Immune profiling suggested immune microenvironment remodelling, characterised by increased memory B cells, activated mast cells, and CD4 + T helper cell subsets, with decreased M2 macrophages, monocytes, and neutrophils. PIK3CG and IL1B were positively associated with adaptive immune-related signals, whereas UACA showed predominantly negative immune correlations. PIK3CG showed moderate and variable discriminative performance, with an area under the curve of 0.775 in the training data set and 0.614 and 0.743 in validation data sets. The MR and MVMR analyses suggested that IRF1- and UACA-mediated increases in FEV1/FVC were associated with lower COPD risk independently of smoking. Additionally, qRT-PCR confirmed PIK3CG up-regulation in COPD lung tissues, whereas IRF1 and UACA showed no remarkable expression changes. Conclusions Our results suggest that PIK3CG is a computationally and experimentally supported biomarker for COPD, while IRF1 and UACA act as genetically implicated regulators of airflow limitation. Together, these findings show the potential importance of PANoptosis-driven immune microenvironmental remodelling as a therapeutic direction warranting further functional validation.

papers.title: Stochastic and Quantum Perspectives on Teleost Immunity: Linking Immunogenetics, Structure, and Biophysics.
papers.authors: Abo-Al-Ela HG.
papers.abstract: Teleost fishes possess highly diverse, lineage-specific pattern-recognition receptor (PRR) repertoires shaped by teleost-specific whole-genome duplication (3R-WGD), subsequent duplication, differential retention, functional divergence, and gene loss. Toll-like, RIG-I-like, and NOD-like receptor families show lineage-specific expansion and, in some cases, adaptive sequence evolution, particularly in regions implicated in ligand recognition. Separately, hydrogen tunneling is supported in specific enzyme reactions, while radical-pair chemistry provides a bounded mechanistic precedent rather than evidence for teleost immune function. This review examines whether teleost PRR diversification creates concrete, testable opportunities for investigating analogous biophysical mechanisms, without assuming that receptor diversity or environmental sensitivity entails non-classical effects. A five-level evidence hierarchy is applied: direct teleost evidence, evidence from other systems, indirect teleost evidence, testable hypothesis, and unsupported or contradicted claim. No direct evidence was identified for a functionally consequential quantum-biological mechanism in teleost immune recognition or signaling. However, increasing genomic, structural, transcriptomic, single-cell, and functional-genomic resolution provides a tractable framework for testing such possibilities. Sequence and structural divergence among PRR paralogs can be evaluated using structure prediction, molecular dynamics, and, where chemically justified, quantum-chemical or QM/MM methods, with uncertainty assessed across stages and experimental validation through ligand binding, signaling, and environmental-response phenotypes. The NADPH-to-flavin hydride-transfer step in an immune effector oxidase is proposed as a chemically defined candidate, not an established teleost tunneling mechanism. Quantum mechanisms therefore remain hypotheses rather than established features of teleost immunity. A falsifiable research roadmap is proposed linking receptor evolution to structure-function relationships, signaling diversity, redox processes, and candidate quantum-sensitive molecular events.

papers.title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
papers.authors: Ye X, Wang Y, Li Y, Zhu H, Li X, Song J.
papers.abstract: Background/objectives Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference. Discussion Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8 + cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported. Conclusions Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Reveal Convergence on a Senescence-Associated B Cell-MIF Signaling Axis in Joint Aging and Osteoarthritis Progression.
papers.authors: Li W, Wang Y, You Y, Cui Y, Liu J, Ma X, Zhu Q, Wu Q, Zhai Z, Lu Z, Dai K, Sun Y.
papers.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) involves age-associated structural and immune changes, yet whether senescence-associated B-cell states contribute to cartilage degeneration remains unclear. Integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of healthy, aged, and OA mouse joints identify reduced B-cell abundance but enrichment of a low-proliferative, inflammatory state with heightened macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) signaling. Cell-cell communication and spatial ligand-receptor analyses identify enhanced predicted MIF-CD74/CD44 interactions in B-cell-associated regions adjacent to cartilage. Constitutive MIF deficiency attenuates senescence-associated B-cell changes, MMP13 induction, and cartilage damage in vivo. Joint-derived B cells from aged and OA mice induce chondrocyte senescence, reduce COL2A1 and HMGB1, and increase FN1 and MMP13 through MIF-dependent paracrine signaling. These effects are suppressed by MIF neutralization and restored by recombinant MIF in MIF-deficient co-cultures. A composite hydrogel carrying quercetin and MIF-siRNA-loaded PLGA microspheres for local co-delivery. The microspheres show gradual siRNA release over 96 h in vitro. In DMM-induced OA, the formulation reduces MIF, P16, and MMP13 signals, restores HMGB1, and preserves cartilage. These findings support a senescence-associated B cell-MIF signaling axis associated with joint aging and chondrocyte dysfunction and provide proof of concept for a local biomaterial-based strategy that attenuates OA-associated changes.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell transcriptomic and experimental analyses identify macrophage-associated STAT3 signaling contributing to ferroptosis-related injury in septic cardiomyopathy.
papers.authors: Qiu S, Dai R, Huang X, Zhu W, Zhang W, Feng L, Yang J, Huo M, Shao H.
papers.abstract: Background Septic cardiomyopathy (SCM) is a major complication of sepsis, but how inflammatory immune cells contribute to ferroptosis-related myocardial injury remains unclear. We investigated ferroptosis-associated transcriptional remodeling in SCM and the functional contribution of macrophage STAT3 signaling. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication analysis, and independent mouse and human transcriptomic cohorts were integrated to characterize ferroptosis-associated changes. Driver and suppressor signatures were analyzed separately. STAT3 was silenced in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages, followed by conditioned-medium transfer to H9C2 cardiomyocytes. Ferroptosis-related injury was evaluated using lipid peroxidation, Fe²⁺ accumulation, molecular markers, Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1) intervention, and an SCM mouse model. Results Ferroptosis-associated transcriptional features showed marked cell-type heterogeneity. Inflammatory macrophages exhibited prominent STAT3-related inflammatory signaling and extensive predicted communication with cardiomyocytes. Independent cohorts revealed context-dependent changes in ferroptosis driver and suppressor programs. Conditioned medium from LPS-stimulated macrophages induced cardiomyocyte injury, lipid peroxidation, Fe²⁺ accumulation, decreased GPX4, and increased ACSL4. Macrophage STAT3 knockdown partially attenuated these changes, reduced inflammatory responses, and altered Cp expression. Fer-1 further alleviated conditioned-medium-induced injury. Consistent ferroptosis-related molecular alterations were observed in SCM mice. Conclusion Macrophage STAT3 signaling contributes to a paracrine inflammatory environment associated with ferroptosis-related cardiomyocyte injury, linking inflammatory macrophages to myocardial injury in SCM.

papers.title: Single-cell proteomics of saliva enables noninvasive cell profiling in oral cancer.
papers.authors: Monteiro do Amaral-Prado H, Miyamoto JG, de Figueiredo D, Malta de Sá Patroni F, Antônio da Rocha Coimbra N, Busso-Lopes AF, Telles GP, Carnielli CM, Granato DC, Câmara GA, Camacho MF, Cardoso EC, De Rossi T, Domingues RR, Pauletti BA, Mores AL, Prado-Ribeiro AC, Brandão TB, Kowalski LP, Santos-Silva AR, Lopes MA, Cervigne NK, Nimtz Rodrigues AA, Maion Casarim AL, Paes Leme AF.
papers.abstract: Single-cell proteomics based on mass spectrometry (SCP) has the potential to resolve cellular heterogeneity in complex microenvironments without requiring prior antibody labeling, yet its application to clinically accessible biofluids remains limited. Here, we established a high-coverage, label-free SCP workflow capable of quantifying up to 5,400 protein groups per cell, as benchmarked using single fresh and cryopreserved HeLa cells. We then applied this workflow to noninvasive saliva and tear fluid samples from healthy donors (n = 398 cells), identifying up to 1,000 and 600 protein groups per cell, respectively. Extending the approach to cryopreserved salivary CD3 + T cells from patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC; n = 526 cells), we quantified up to 1,600 protein groups per cell and identified proteomic cell states associated with immune remodeling. Furthermore, exploratory trajectory analyses suggested continuous proteomic state transitions that were consistent with publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets. Together, these results establish a workflow for single-cell proteomic profiling of clinically accessible and noninvasive biofluids and provide a framework for investigating cellular heterogeneity in translational and clinical research.

papers.title: Lightweight Instance Segmentation Network for Microscopic Images of Suspension-Cultured B Cells Integrating Edge Priors and Multi-Scale Attention.
papers.authors: Tang A, Li Z, Gong W, Song Y, Du X, Kabika T, Liu Z, Liao G, Nie L.
papers.abstract: Precise single-cell analysis is important for life sciences and precision medicine. In antibody drug discovery and immunotherapy, automated segmentation and quantitative analysis of suspension-cultured B cells in label-free bright-field microscopic images can support image-based characterization of cell populations under the recorded culture conditions. However, accurate segmentation remains challenging because of weak boundary gradients, heterogeneous cell sizes, background interference, and high-density clustering. Existing deep learning models may also face a trade-off between segmentation performance and model compactness, which can limit their use in resource-constrained automated microscopy systems. To address these challenges, we propose EPMSA-Net, a lightweight instance segmentation network that integrates edge priors and multi-scale attention for B-cell image analysis. The proposed framework incorporates two complementary structures: the Edge-Aware Feature Preservation (EAFP) module supplements weak boundary-related and local spatial cues during early feature extraction, whereas the Multi-Scale Contextual Attention (MSCA) module subsequently models multi-scale contextual information and recalibrates downstream feature responses. Evaluation on the current suspension-cultured B-cell dataset yielded an F1-score of 94.44% ± 0.53% and an Aggregated Jaccard Index (AJI) of 89.87% ± 0.78% over five independent training runs, with a parameter count of 3.276 M. Density-stratified evaluation showed relatively small F1-score variation across the predefined low-, medium-, and high-density subsets, with a mean CV F1 of 0.84% ± 0.13%. The resulting instance masks were further used to calculate image-level cell count and segmented area ratio (SAR). These results indicate that EPMSA-Net achieves competitive segmentation performance with a compact model size on the current dataset. Further validation across independent culture batches, imaging systems, and hardware platforms is required to evaluate its broader applicability and deployment performance.

papers.title: Dissecting cell-type-specific genetic associations between colorectal cancer liability and thrombotic risk in peripheral blood immune cells.
papers.authors: Ying J, Ling T, Fang Z, Zhang C, Bao Y, Tang J.
papers.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether CRC-associated thrombotic susceptibility includes cell-specific inherited regulatory components in peripheral blood remains unclear. To investigate associations between CRC genetic liability and VTE-related outcomes within peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) regulatory contexts. We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR). Prioritized signals were further examined in single-cell RNA-seq datasets and bulk transcriptomes. Conventional MR showed no clear evidence that CRC liability increased VTE, DVT, or PE risk, and LD Score regression detected no significant genome-wide genetic correlation. In contrast, csMR identified nominal, cell-context-dependent associations. B intermediate cells were prioritized across VTE (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32), DVT (OR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.08-1.57), and PE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49), while CD14 + monocytes and CD4 + central memory T cells received additional support from downstream single-cell analyses. Gene-level analyses prioritized LAMA5, LIMA1, and TRIM28 in these respective cell contexts. In bulk blood, RPS21 showed consistent disease-associated expression patterns and discriminated VTE patients from healthy controls in an external dataset (AUC, 0.865; 95% CI, 0.800-0.923). These findings suggest that genetic overlap between CRC liability and thrombotic phenotypes may be localized to selected PBMC regulatory contexts rather than broadly detectable genome-wide. Among the prioritized signals, B intermediate cells showed the most consistent csMR associations across VTE, DVT, and PE. The cell-gene pairs, together with RPS21, warrant independent genetic, functional, and prospective validation as candidates for studying peripheral immune regulation and blood-based markers of CRC-associated thrombosis.

papers.title: Tumor-derived amyloid-β drives TREM2 + macrophages immunosuppression in cholangiocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Li X, Qian R, Li Y, Xu X, Luo Z, Lin H, Zhu G, Wang G, Gao Y, Liu C, Liu F, Lin Y, Zhang Y, Tian X, Liu Q, Jiang S, Ma C.
papers.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is an aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options. In this study, we explored the role of TREM2 + tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) in modulating the immune microenvironment and their impact on anti-PD-1 therapy. Using single-cell RNA sequencing data and immunohistochemical analysis, we identified a significant upregulation of TREM2 in TAMs in human CCA, correlating with decreased CD8 + T cell infiltration and poor prognosis. TREM2 deficiency in a mouse model of CCA led to a reprogramming of TAMs to a pro-inflammatory phenotype, with a marked increase in CD86 + macrophages and a significant reduction in CD206 + macrophages. This phenotypic shift enhanced the recruitment and activity of CD8 + T cells, driving a potent pro-inflammatory immune response. Additionally, we uncovered that Aβ produced by CCA cells contributes to TAM polarization through TREM2/PI3K/AKT1 signaling pathway. Blocking Aβ signaling further augmented TAM reprogramming and CD8 + T cell infiltration. The combination of TREM2 deletion and Aβ inhibition significantly enhanced the efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy, resulting in reduced tumor growth, increased survival, and improved overall therapeutic outcomes in both subcutaneous and hydrodynamic tail vein CCA models. These findings suggest that targeting TREM2 and Aβ in conjunction with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy holds promise as a novel therapeutic strategy for CCA.

papers.title: Myeloid integrin α9β1 deficiency protects alveolar bone by remodeling the immune microenvironment of periodontitis.
papers.authors: Xu S, Li W, Bai Z, Yang S, Zhu W, Li J, Xia J.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by microbial infection that can lead to periodontal tissue damage and alveolar bone resorption. Macrophages contribute to the regulation of periodontal inflammation and local tissue homeostasis, but the role of integrin α9β1 in these processes remains unclear. Here, we combined analysis of human gingival single-cell transcriptomic data, a mouse model of myeloid cell-specific conditional Itga9 deletion, in vitro experiments with bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs), and conditioned-medium experiments in gingival fibroblasts to investigate how α9β1 affects the immune microenvironment and bone destruction in periodontitis. ITGA9 was highly expressed in human gingival macrophages and was further upregulated in periodontitis. Itga9 deletion altered the basal transcriptional state of BMMs and their response to Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg), with reduced TNF production, downregulation of inflammation-related gene sets, and lower AKT and S6 phosphorylation following Pg stimulation. In vivo, myeloid Itga9 deletion reduced periodontal tissue damage and alveolar bone loss and was accompanied by changes in local immune cell composition and fibroblast-associated communication networks. Gene sets related to skeletal development, ossification, and extracellular matrix (ECM)-receptor interactions were positively enriched in fibroblasts. Further in vitro experiments showed that conditioned medium from Pg-stimulated KO BMMs was less inhibitory to gingival fibroblast mineralization than that from Pg-stimulated Het BMMs, as reflected by higher expression of mineralization-related genes, greater alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, and increased mineralized nodule formation. These findings suggest that myeloid integrin α9β1 contributes to the regulation of immune and stromal cell functions in periodontitis and that targeting this receptor may help reduce inflammation-associated bone destruction and support the mineralization potential of gingival fibroblasts.

papers.title: Single-Cell RNA sequencing analysis of cellular heterogeneity and microenvironment-driven signaling networks in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.authors: Ching LJ, Wang CH, Lo WL, Cheng YJ, Ou-Yang H, Lan YT, Huang PI, Chen YW, Yao YH, Chiou SH, Yang YP, Tsai PH, Ko PS.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) exhibits cellular heterogeneity that complicates tumor micro-environment (TME) characterization. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) with BayesPrism bulk transcriptomic deconvolution to compare cellular composition by cytogenetic risk (favorable versus adverse). scRNA-seq identified immune and malignant hematopoietic populations, including leukemia stem cell (LSC) and granulocyte-monocyte-progenitor clusters, with recurrent alterations involving chromosomes 5, 7, and 8. TCGA-LAML deconvolution reconstructed cell-type-resolved profiles and linked adverse-risk AML to poorer overall survival. CellChat showed expanded cell-cell communication in adverse-risk disease involving SPP1, CXCL, GRN, TENASCIN, VCAM, and WNT signaling, particularly in leukemic stem-like and megakaryocytic compartments. Pathway analysis implicated differentiation arrest and immune exhaustion. In-silico repurposing nominated belinostat: ASGARD ranked it the top HDAC inhibitor, and scRANK characterized its HDAC1-centered target network. Gene-set analysis showed consistent interferon-gamma responses across key cell populations. These findings provide a transcriptome-based, hypothesis-generating framework linking cellular heterogeneity, microenvironmental signaling, and therapeutic vulnerabilities in adverse-risk AML.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
papers.authors: Wu Q, Hu J, Abuliezi N, Sun Y, Wu Y, Dun X.
papers.abstract: Abstract Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion, and mesenchymal stem cell-treated samples. In this exploratory dataset, the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion samples showed relatively greater representation of inflammatory and antigen-presenting microglial states and elevated expression of selected microglial state-associated genes, including Slfn4, Apoe, and Gpnmb. In the corresponding exploratory comparison, the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample showed relatively greater representation of homeostatic-associated and Lgals3/Spp1-enriched microglial states and lower expression of several inflammatory-associated genes. Spatial mapping further revealed regionally restricted expression of microglial and neuronal markers within the injured tissue. Excitatory neurons displayed preliminary mesenchymal stem cell-associated transcriptional patterns involving mitochondrial transcripts, oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic signaling, calcium-related functions, and apoptosis/autophagy-associated pathways. CellChat analysis computationally predicted relatively high levels of tumor necrosis factor, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand, and complement signaling in the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion sample, whereas the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample had relatively high levels of predicted activity of neuregulin, pleiotrophin and selected semaphorin. Together, these integrated datasets provide a hypothesis-generating framework linking microglial state remodeling, neuronal metabolic and synaptic programs, and predicted neuroimmune communication patterns after ischemic stroke. Because each omics condition or time point was represented by one biological sample, all the transcriptomic findings should be considered preliminary and exploratory and should be validated in independently replicated cohorts.

papers.title: Fibroblast-immune crosstalk in central nervous system injury and repair: Spatiotemporal control of barrier restoration, inflammation resolution and fibrotic scarring.
papers.authors: Li P, Zhang X, Zhang H, Liu L, Chai Y, Zhang S, Chen X.
papers.abstract: Abstract Central nervous system repair after injury is increasingly understood as a spatially and temporally organized process involving vascular disruption, immune-cell recruitment, extracellular matrix remodeling and reconstruction of glial-stromal borders. Within this process, central nervous system fibroblasts are not merely matrix-producing scar cells, but injury-responsive stromal organizers positioned at key neuroimmune interfaces, including the meninges, perivascular spaces and choroid plexus. Recent single-cell, spatial and lineage-resolved studies indicate that anatomically distinct fibroblast populations undergo phase-specific state transitions after traumatic brain injury, stroke, and spinal cord injury. During the acute phase, activated fibroblasts and myofibroblast-like states contribute to lesion containment, barrier restoration and protection of surrounding parenchyma. In the subacute and chronic phases, fibroblasts interact dynamically with neutrophils, microglia, macrophages, lymphocytes and innate lymphoid cells to shape immune-cell positioning, inflammatory resolution, vascular repair and, when unresolved, persistent fibrotic scarring. This review synthesizes emerging evidence on fibroblast-immune crosstalk in central nervous system injury, with particular emphasis on the unresolved origins of injury-responsive stromal cells, lesion-topology-dependent fibroblast recruitment, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 12-mediated lymphocyte organization, choroid plexus fibroblast-group 2 innate lymphoid cell niches, and fibroblast contributions to blood-brain barrier and vascular repair. Rather than framing fibrotic scars as uniformly detrimental, we propose that central nervous system fibrosis reflects context-dependent fibroblast states that can be either reparative or maladaptive depending on timing, anatomical niche and immune milieu. Therapeutic strategies should therefore avoid indiscriminate fibroblast depletion and instead aim to preserve early protective functions while selectively modulating chronic fibroblast-immune circuits that sustain inflammation and inhibit regeneration.

papers.title: Divergent glial PANoptosis-related signatures and astrocyte-centered network remodeling in retinal ischemia-reperfusion injury: Single-cell RNAsequencing analysis.
papers.authors: Yan W, Lu S, Wang L, Wan H, Tan Y, Zhang Q, Wan X, Huang Y, Liu N, Wang H, He Y, Xiong K.
papers.abstract: Abstract Retinal ischemia-reperfusion injury is a major cause of irreversible vision loss. Although microglia, astrocytes, and Müller glia are key responders, how they coordinate their responses at single-cell resolution remains incompletely understood. Therefore, this study investigated differences in PANoptosis-related signatures among glial cells and astrocyte-centered network remodeling in retinal ischemia-reperfusion injury. In this study, we established a high-intraocular-pressurerat model and performed single-cell RNA-sequencing on control and injured retinas. Subcluster analysis, cell death pathway profiling, and CellChat-based communication inference were integrated to resolve glial heterogeneity, death programs, and communication networks. The results suggested a trend toward compositional remodeling in microglia, astrocytes, and Müller glia, characterized by a trend toward reduction of homeostatic subcluster and a trend toward expansion of reactive subcluster. The three glial types displayed divergent PANoptosis-related transcriptional patterns. Microglia showed concurrent upregulation of pyroptotic, apoptotic, and necroptotic markers together with the upstream sensor transcripts Aim2, Pycard, and Nlrp12. Astrocytes exhibited selective upregulation of NLRC5transcripts but ASC remained unchanged. Müller glia displayed predominantly apoptotic features. CellChat analysis inferred an astrocyte-centered remodeling of the glial communication network, in which microglia lost their dominant position as senders of inflammatory and trophic signals, while astrocytes showed increased signaling associated with damage sensing, inflammatory output, neurotrophic support, and immune recruitment. These findings suggest that astrocyte-centered network remodeling may represent a potential target for further investigation in retinal ischemia-reperfusion injury.

papers.title: Citizen Science Gamers Enable Automated Flow Cytometry Gating Through Machine Learning.
papers.authors: Montante S, Yokosawa D, Li L, Butyaev A, Malek M, Movassaghi R, Michalchuk Q, Hsu CJ, Shmil D, Rahim A, Cossarizza A, Esteban JB, Erhart K, Finnbogason B, Kelion G, Leifsson H, Rivers J, Ecker D, Szantner A, Waldispühl J, Brinkman RR.
papers.abstract: Machine learning can greatly accelerate biomedical research but is fundamentally constrained by the scarcity of high-quality labeled data. We introduce a scalable data-generation framework based on citizen science and apply it to automated flow cytometry gating, a foundational but subjective step in immunology that limits reproducibility. Using the massively multiplayer online game EVE Online, 839,199 de-identified player accounts analyzed 52,000 plots, from which stringent quality control produced 31,703 consensus annotations for model training. Leveraging these data, we developed flowMagic, a machine learning framework for automated gating. Evaluated on 92,203 bivariate plots with standardized reference gates spanning 79 immune populations, the template model outperformed the generalized model, achieving 90% and 65% agreement for large and low-abundance populations, respectively, compared with 78% and 42% for the generalized model. These results show that expert-provided templates currently provide the highest agreement, while the citizen-science-trained generalized model enables gating without gate-specific templates but remains limited by the absence of expert-curated examples for complex, low-abundance or context-dependent gates. Both model types reproduced biologically meaningful patterns, including neutrophil dynamics in COVID-19 patients and immune development in newborns. Together, these results establish citizen-science annotation as a scalable strategy for generating training data that complements, rather than replaces, expert input in automated flow cytometry gating.
papers.venue: Cytometry. Part A : the journal of the International Society for Analytical Cytology

papers.title: SprintX: mitigating data scarcity in antibody design via synthetic structural prior knowledge dataset.
papers.authors: Heo R, Lee D, Jung J, Kim BJ, Park C.
papers.abstract: Structure-based artificial intelligence (AI)-driven antibody design is increasingly important for therapeutic development, yet progress has been hindered by the scarcity of high-quality antibody-antigen complex structures for model training. To alleviate this bottleneck, we introduce SprintX (Structural Prior for Antibody-Antigen CompleXes), a large-scale AlphaFold3-derived synthetic dataset designed to provide structural prior knowledge for antibody-antigen modeling. Unlike conventional docking-based synthesis pipelines, SprintX uses AlphaFold3 to generate antigen-conditioned candidate complex-structure predictions from sampled antibody sequences paired with selected antigens, without imposing predefined binding-site or pose constraints. Candidate structures were ranked to select one representative structure per antibody-antigen pair before terminal trimming and multistage quality control. To improve reliability and learning stability, we applied a multi-stage quality-control pipeline integrating global confidence metrics, stereochemical validation, and interface-level contact analysis. SprintX recapitulated key geometric characteristics and physicochemical regularities of experimentally resolved antibody-antigen complexes while filtering out structurally unstable or implausible synthetic outputs. Across downstream tasks including antibody generation, computational binding-affinity prediction, and binding-interface prediction, models pretrained with SprintX showed meaningful improvements in structural plausibility and competitive performance on computational binding-affinity and binding-interface prediction benchmarks. These results support SprintX not as a substitute for experimentally resolved complexes, but as a complementary source of structural prior knowledge for structure-aware antibody modeling. Finally, we release SprintX as an openly accessible resource to facilitate data-efficient learning for AI-driven antibody design.

papers.title: VAMP5 Mediates Sevoflurane-Induced Immune Modulation in Cervical Cancer: A Clinical Translational Study.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Dong X, Yu T, Li H, Yuan X.
papers.abstract: Background Sevoflurane, a commonly used inhaled anesthetic, has been implicated in modulating tumor biology and perioperative immune responses, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study aims to investigate whether sevoflurane regulates key immune-related genes in cervical cancer patients undergoing laparoscopic radical hysterectomy (LRH) and to explore the clinical relevance of such regulation. Methods Based on prior RNA-seq screening, we established a two-step validation framework to identify sevoflurane-regulated genes in a clinical cohort. A total of 116 cervical cancer patients undergoing LRH were enrolled, including 70 who received sevoflurane anesthesia and 46 who received propofol anesthesia. Peripheral blood samples were collected at five perioperative time points. mRNA expression levels of candidate genes were measured by qRT-PCR, lymphocyte subsets were analyzed by flow cytometry, and VAMP5 protein expression was assessed by intracellular staining. Bioinformatics analyses were performed using TCGA data to evaluate associations between candidate genes and tumor immune infiltration. Results MAP3K7 and VAMP5 were validated as sevoflurane-downregulated targets, showing sustained suppression postoperatively compared to the propofol group. VAMP5 expression correlated significantly with tumor progression and immune cell infiltration in cervical cancer, particularly CD8 + T-cells, B-cells, and macrophages. Among sevoflurane-treated patients, those with lower VAMP5 expression exhibited delayed postoperative recovery of CD8 + T-cell counts at 48 and 72 h after surgery, whereas no such difference was observed for other lymphocyte subsets. Conclusions This study identify VAMP5 as a novel molecular link between anesthetic choice and immune modulation, suggesting that sevoflurane may influence perioperative immune recovery through vesicle-associated mechanisms, with potential implications for optimizing anesthesia strategies to improve oncologic outcomes.

papers.title: Innate sensor responses set a supra-unitary threshold for viral replication.
papers.authors: Mukai K, Jia D, Panigrahi M, Tayman T, Brogden G, Chen YH, Haque N, Arora G, Mutterperl JE, Poe I, Zhang C, Islam Z, Holewinski R, Andresson T, Wu D, Piszczek G, Marcotrigiano J, Hogg JR, De Ravin SS, Malik NS, Nath A, Viktorova E, Zimina A, Belov GA, Bayyurt-Kocabaş B, Altan-Bonnet G, Altan-Bonnet N.
papers.abstract: Cells resist viral infection by triggering rapid and sensitive innate immune responses, initiated by cytoplasmic viral sensor proteins (CyVSP), retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I), melanoma differentiation-associated protein 5 (MDA-5), and protein kinase R (PKR). Our single-cell analysis reveals that viral replication requires a supra-unitary viral genome input, significantly more than one, which we define as the virion input threshold for replication (VITREP). This threshold varies depending on viruses and cell types, independently of viral protein synthesis. Through mathematical modeling and experimental testing, we uncover that supra-unitary viral genome quantities activate negative feedback regulators (NFR) of CyVSP, including death-associated protein kinase 1 (DAPK1), Rio kinase 3 (RIOK3), and protein phosphatase 2 regulatory subunit alpha (PPP2R2A), that suppress innate immune responses and allow replication. We validate key predictions of our model, namely that downregulating NFR reduces replication, whereas upregulating NFR or coinfecting cells promotes replication. Together, these findings reveal a fundamental mechanism governing viral infectivity and tissue tropism.

papers.title: Quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly reveals a non-linear association with 30-day mortality in sepsis: a proof-of-concept pilot study.
papers.authors: Mehl F, Chedjou WJ, Witowski A, Rump K, Dyck B, Bergmann L, Putensen C, Henzler D, Adamzik M, Koos B, Thon P, Rahmel T.
papers.abstract: Background Direct, cell-resolved quantification of NLRP3 inflammasome activation in clinical patients has not been feasible. Previous studies have relied on indirect surrogates such as downstream cytokines, which are influenced by inflammasome-independent pathways and systemic clearance kinetics, potentially explaining the inconsistent prognostic findings reported in the literature. We applied a proximity ligation assay (PLA) to directly visualise NLRP3-caspase-1 complex formation in peripheral blood mononuclear cells of septic patients, providing a cell-specific, in situ readout of inflammasome assembly at the single-cell level. Methods In this prospective, multicentre proof-of-concept pilot study, 78 patients fulfilling Sepsis-3 criteria were enrolled across three university hospitals. The PLA was validated in THP-1-derived macrophages against established readouts of canonical inflammasome activation prior to clinical application. Patients were stratified into low (n = 28), intermediate (n = 23), and high (n = 27) NLRP3 inflammasome activity groups. Results Median age was 64 years (IQR: 56-78), 63% were male, and median Sequential Organ Failure Assessment score was 8 (IQR: 4-12). Baseline characteristics, disease severity scores, and routine inflammatory biomarkers did not differ across activity groups. Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed a non-linear pattern of 30-day survival, with the most favourable outcomes in the intermediate activity group. Both low and high activity were associated with increased mortality (log-rank p = 0.003). In adjusted Cox regression, low inflammasome activity (HR 7.88, 95% CI 1.79-34.65; p = 0.006) and high inflammasome activity (HR 4.35, 95% CI 1.01-19.88; p = 0.048) remained associated with 30-day mortality. Modelling PLA activity as a continuous variable using restricted cubic splines confirmed a significant non-linear association with 30-day mortality, independent of the tertile-based categorisation (p for non-linearity = 0.015). Conclusions This proof-of-concept pilot study demonstrates that direct in situ quantification of NLRP3-caspase-1 complex assembly is feasible in septic patients and reveals a non-linear association with 30-day survival. These findings indicate that PLA-based profiling captures immune heterogeneity beyond routine inflammatory biomarkers. Larger independent cohorts are needed to validate these findings before clinical application or patient stratification can be considered.

papers.title: Capsanthin at the crossroads of arthritis: from molecular mechanisms to therapeutic avenues.
papers.authors: Islam I, Dey P.
papers.abstract: Arthritis, particularly rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and osteoarthritis (OA), is a multifactorial musculoskeletal disorder characterized by chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, immune dysregulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, extracellular matrix degradation and progressive cartilage and bone destruction. Although conventional therapies, including disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, biologics and JAK inhibitors, have improved disease management, their long-term use is frequently associated with adverse effects, therapeutic resistance and incomplete prevention of irreversible joint degeneration, necessitating safer multitarget therapeutic strategies. Capsicum species contain diverse bioactive constituents, including capsanthin, capsorubin, capsaicin, dihydrocapsaicin, β-carotene and zeaxanthin. Among these, capsanthin, found in Capsicum species, has attracted considerable interest because of its potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, and metabolic regulatory properties. This review comprehensively evaluates the potential anti-arthritic activity of capsanthin, with particular emphasis on signaling networks implicated in joint inflammation, oxidative stress, immune dysregulation, and extracellular matrix degradation, including CB2, NF-κB, Nrf2/HO-1, MAPK, PI3K/Akt, and JAK/STAT pathways. The available evidence is critically distinguished according to capsanthin-specific findings, arthritis-related mechanisms, and supportive evidence from other carotenoids or disease models. Additionally, modulation of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) and ADAMTS aggrecanases involved in cartilage degradation and extracellular matrix remodeling is critically discussed. Current preclinical evidence indicates that capsanthin suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokine production, restores cellular redox homeostasis, attenuates oxidative stress-mediated signaling, and preserves cartilage integrity through coordinated regulation of interconnected molecular networks. Emerging computational approaches, including network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, artificial intelligence-assisted drug discovery, and multi-omics technologies, are also highlighted to accelerate target identification, mechanism and future clinical translation.

papers.title: Exploring Gut Microbial Metabolic Signatures Associated with the Gut-Lung Axis in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Yuan JQ, Zhong JY, Hu TC, Wang Z.
papers.abstract: Objective The gut-lung axis (GLA) is increasingly recognized as a biological communication pathway relevant to lung cancer. However, the potential molecular associations between gut microbial metabolites and lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain incompletely understood. Methods By integrating public databases, including gutMGene, GeneCards, and TCGA, with computational tools such as WGCNA, STRING, and CIBERSORT, candidate genes and gut microbiota-derived metabolites potentially associated with LUAD were identified. A microbiota-metabolite-targets-pathway (MMTP) interaction network was constructed, followed by functional enrichment, immune infiltration analysis, miRNA-target prediction, and drug-likeness analyses. Results Among the 12 key targets identified, JUN, IL6, and CXCL8 were prioritized as core genes. These targets mainly involved miRNA-related processes and immune pathways like IL-17 signaling, Toll-like receptor, and Th17 differentiation. Immune infiltration showed that core gene expression correlated with specific immune cell patterns, indicating inflammatory and immunosuppressive features of the tumor microenvironment (TME). The MMTP network further suggested that several gut microbial metabolites, including butyrate, propionate, acetate, succinate, 3-indolepropionic acid, and trimethylamine N-oxide, may be associated with core gene-related pathways. In silico drug-likeness and toxicity predictions indicated that these metabolites generally met basic Lipinski-based criteria; however, several predicted toxicity signals, particularly human hepatotoxicity, warrant cautious interpretation. Conclusion Key gut microbial metabolites may be linked to LUAD progression via inflammatory and immune pathways involving JUN, IL6, and CXCL8, along with miRNA regulatory processes. These findings offer a bioinformatics framework for understanding GLA-related molecular links in LUAD and may help find biomarkers or metabolites for further study.

papers.title: Supramolecular assembly and membrane anchoring alter variant-induced SARS-CoV-2 Spike conformational dynamics.
papers.authors: Gramm AJ, Braet SM, Srinivasu BY, Venkatakrishnan V, Bass EJ, Kearns FL, Amaro RE, Stahelin RV, Wales TE, Anand GS.
papers.abstract: Viral surface glycoproteins function within crowded, membrane-anchored supramolecular assemblies, yet their dynamics are often inferred from soluble, engineered ectodomains. For SARS-CoV-2 Spike (S), this distinction is especially important because variant mutations evolved in the context of intact virions, not engineered trimers. Here, we combined cyclic ion mobility mass spectrometry (CIM-MS) for hydrogen deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDXMS) with computational weighted ensemble molecular dynamic (WE-MD) simulations to compare the conformational effects of SARS-CoV-2 mutations in two S protein constructs: soluble recombinant 2P S and full-length S displayed in virus-like particles (VLPs). Our results reveal that membrane anchoring and virion-like assembly substantially dampen global dynamic changes produced by variant mutations. In VLP S, D614G induced decreased dynamics across interprotomer contacts, whereas Omicron BA.1 mutations systematically reversed this decrease in dynamics in the S1 domain while preserving decreased dynamics near the fusion machinery. These effects are more spatially constrained than those observed in recombinant 2P S. Comparison of the 2 constructs further reveals that 2P substitutions alter native interprotomer communication. Recombinant S shows a predominantly fast-exchanging population in the receptor binding domain (RBD) hinge region, consistent with disruption of hydrogen-bonding and salt bridge networks that couple RBD motion to the trimer core. Thus, recombinant S captures important structural features of S without recapitulating the native conformational ensemble presented on virions. Together, these results show that the supramolecular context of S reshapes the conformational dynamics of variant evolution with direct implications for epitope presentation, antibody recognition, and interpretation of recombinant S structural studies.

papers.title: Aromaticity at spike position 456 affects functional immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant receptor-binding domain.
papers.authors: Peng D, Chen Z, Fu M, Hong W, Dai M, Zeng H, Lin S, Lei H, Yang J, Shi J, Huang X, Ye C, Qin F, Zhang Y, Hao Y, Wang B, Ren W, Chen L, Liu J, Alu A, Lu Y, Du X, Li J, Shi H, Wei Y, Chen Y, Lu S, He C, Lu G, Wei X.
papers.abstract: The recurrent emergence of the F456L substitution in SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sublineages has been associated with immune evasion, yet its impact on vaccine-induced immune responses remains poorly understood. Using a trimeric RBD-HR subunit vaccine platform, we investigated how residue 456 influences the functional immunogenicity of the receptor-binding domain (RBD). We found that the F456L substitution markedly reduced neutralizing antibody responses against multiple SARS-CoV-2 variants, despite maintaining comparable levels of total antigen-specific IgG, indicating a selective impairment of functional immunogenicity rather than overall antigenicity. Single-cell RNA sequencing and B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire analyses further revealed that the F456L mutation weakened germinal center responses, reduced clonal expansion, and impaired repertoire remodeling of antigen-specific B cells. Structural modeling, biolayer interferometry, and calcium flux assays demonstrated that aromatic residues at position 456 promote effective germline BCR recognition and activation. Importantly, replacing the non-aromatic leucine residue with aromatic amino acids, including tyrosine or tryptophan, restored the neutralizing antibody-eliciting capacity of the antigen. Together, these findings identify aromaticity at residue 456 as a critical determinant of RBD functional immunogenicity and demonstrate how a single amino acid substitution can reshape B-cell responses and antibody quality. This work provides important insights for rational vaccine antigen design and advances our understanding of how site-specific mutations regulate antiviral immunity.

papers.title: Microglial perturbation in heavy metal-induced neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration: mechanisms, phenotypic plasticity, and therapeutic prospects.
papers.authors: Oria RS, Esomonu UG, Sunday KI, Oge PA.
papers.abstract: Heavy metal exposure has emerged as a significant environmental contributor to neurodegenerative disease, and a substantial body of mechanistic evidence implicates microglia in the pathological cascades that follow. Lead, cadmium, arsenic, manganese, copper, cobalt, mercury, and zinc disrupt central nervous system homeostasis through multiple cellular targets, but the resident innate immune cells of the brain are well placed to translate these insults into sustained neuroinflammation. Evidence for this critical narrative review was assembled through a purposive search of PubMed, MEDLINE, and Google Scholar for mechanistically informative studies reporting glial endpoints, with reference lists searched by hand and no systematic protocol applied. This review synthesizes current understanding of how individual metals engage microglial signaling networks, with particular attention to oxidative stress, NF-κB activation, NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, MAPK cascades, and suppression of the Nrf2 antioxidant axis. We examine the phenotypic spectrum that extends well beyond the classical M1/M2 dichotomy, including disease-associated microglia, lipid-droplet-accumulating microglia, and interferon-responsive states, and consider how metal-specific signatures map onto these transcriptional programs. Manganese-driven inflammasome assembly, cadmium-induced mitochondrial impairment, lead-mediated disruption of calcium homeostasis, and mercury-evoked autophagic dysfunction are discussed as illustrative examples of mechanistic divergence within a common neuroinflammatory framework. Glial responses to metal mixtures, which better represent real exposure than single-element designs, are considered separately, and the evidence for greater-than-additive effects is appraised. Downstream consequences for astrocyte reactivity, blood-brain barrier integrity, synaptic remodeling, and neuronal viability are placed in the context of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Therapeutic avenues are appraised, including chelation, natural antioxidants, NLRP3 inhibitors, TREM2 modulation, and microglial replacement strategies. Methodological constraints, particularly the overreliance on BV-2 cells and acute high-dose exposure paradigms, are critically considered. The review concludes by identifying priorities for translational research, including longitudinal human cohort studies, single-cell transcriptomic profiling of metal-exposed microglia, and the development of region-specific exposure models that better reflect chronic environmental realities.
papers.venue: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine

papers.title: SLC2A1 promotes chemo-immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma by modulating the AKT signaling pathway.
papers.authors: Ruan J, Zhao M, Yuan Y, Zhong J.
papers.abstract: Chemo-immunotherapy has become a standard treatment for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), yet the development of dual resistance to platinum-based chemotherapy and PD-1/PD-L1 blockade severely limits durable clinical benefit. This study aimed to identify a unified molecular regulator that concurrently drives chemoresistance and immune evasion. scRNA-seq of LUAD clinical cohorts was performed to characterize resistance-associated malignant subpopulations, followed by integrative bioinformatics analyses to screen key drivers. Clinical specimen validation and functional experiments, including CCK-8 assays, flow cytometry, transwell migration and western blotting, were conducted to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. We identified a malignant subcluster enriched in non-responsive patients and determined SLC2A1 as the unique overlapping candidate linked to therapeutic failure. Elevated SLC2A1 expression correlated with poor prognosis and enhanced AKT phosphorylation levels. Functionally, SLC2A1 promoted cisplatin resistance, suppressed apoptosis, increased migratory capacity, and upregulated PD-L1 expression, all of which were substantially reversed by AKT inhibition. Notably, this study suggests a previously underappreciated non-canonical role of SLC2A1 as an upstream modulator that coordinates the AKT-PD-L1 axis, thereby potentially integrating chemotherapy resistance and immune escape into a single regulatory framework. These findings provide mechanistic insight into dual refractory LUAD and establish the SLC2A1/AKT axis as a promising therapeutic vulnerability for precision intervention.

papers.title: IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines induce astrocyte programs that support antigen-dependent CD4 + T cell restimulation.
papers.authors: Fisher TM, Limone F, Smith MD, Wright C, Kukanja P, Lu P, Limberg KC, Pirjanian N, Zulueta J, Fossati V, Iwasaki A, Calabresi PA, Liddelow SA.
papers.abstract: Astrocyte contributions to CNS antigen presentation remain poorly defined. We show that interferon gamma (IFN-γ, the sole type II interferon), with proinflammatory cytokines, induces astrocytes to express components mediating attraction of and antigen presentation to CD4 + T cells. Re-analysis of astrocyte-enriched single-cell sequencing from bacterial mimetic-injected mice revealed a transcriptionally distinct, IFN-responsive astrocyte population enriched for antigen-presentation genes 24 h after peripheral immune challenge. In vivo, type II major histocompatibility complex (MHC-II + )GFAP + astrocytes localize to the brain surface across multiple mouse models of neuroinflammation and in human neurological disease tissue. In vitro, purified astrocytes stimulated with IFN-γ and proinflammatory cytokines expressed MHC-II, costimulatory molecules, and lymphocyte-recruiting chemokines, and in co-culture supported rapid antigen-dependent expansion of previously activated CD4 + T cells. Human iPSC-derived CNS cultures showed equivalent induction of antigen-presentation machinery in human astrocytes following inflammatory cytokine stimulation. These findings define a cytokine-induced astrocyte state expressing antigen-presentation machinery at neuroimmune interfaces that can support local CD4 + T cell responses.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell transcriptomics reveals miR-941 targets CLDN4 to inhibit malignant progression of thyroid cancer through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
papers.authors: Zhou J, Fu T, Huang G, Luo G, Wang C, Wang Y, Ding Z, Hu X, Li Y, Li Z.
papers.abstract: Claudin-4 (CLDN4), a key tight junction protein, has been implicated in tumor progression; however, its functional role and regulatory mechanisms in thyroid cancer remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the contribution of CLDN4 to malignant progression and its interaction with the tumor-immune microenvironment. Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were integrated to identify CLDN4-associated malignant epithelial subpopulations. CLDN4 expression was validated in 25 paired papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) tissues by qRT-PCR, western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Functional assays were performed using CLDN4-overexpressing and CLDN4-knockdown B-CPAP and TPC-1 cells. The miR-941-CLDN4 interaction was verified by luciferase reporter assays. PI3K/AKT signaling and macrophage polarization were evaluated in vitro, and tumor growth was assessed in a xenograft mouse model. A CLDN4-high epithelial subpopulation was identified and associated with advanced tumor stage and PI3K/AKT activation. CLDN4 was upregulated in PTC tissues, whereas miR-941 was downregulated. High CLDN4 expression correlated with larger tumor size, lymphatic metastasis, and vascular migration. CLDN4 overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, colony formation, and apoptosis resistance, whereas knockdown produced the opposite effects. miR-941 directly targeted CLDN4 and attenuated its oncogenic effects. CLDN4 activated PI3K/AKT signaling, while PI3K inhibition reversed these phenotypes. CLDN4 also promoted M2 macrophage polarization and suppressed M1 polarization. In vivo, CLDN4 enhanced tumor growth, which was inhibited by PI3K blockade. miR-941 suppresses CLDN4 to inhibit PTC progression through modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway. These findings provide mechanistic insights into tumor progression and immune microenvironment remodeling, highlighting CLDN4 as a potential therapeutic target.
papers.venue: Journal of cell communication and signaling

papers.title: Integrative Multiomics Mendelian Randomization Prioritizes Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress-Related Genes Associated With Gastric Cancer Risk.
papers.authors: Yang D, Liu Y, Meng X, Wang C, Yu Z, Zhang T.
papers.abstract: Background Emerging research indicates connections between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and gastric cancer (GC), but related genetic factors remain unclear. This study is aimed at prioritizing ER stress-related genes associated with GC risk using multiomics data. Methods We integrated GC GWAS data from FinnGen (discovery) and United Kingdom Biobank (replication) cohorts with QTL datasets, including mQTLs, eQTLs, and pQTLs. Summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) and colocalization analyses were performed to prioritize candidate genes, followed by characterization using transcriptomic profiling (GSE118916), methylation-expression correlation analysis (TCGA-STAD), and single-cell RNA-seq analysis (GSE270680). Results SMR analyses identified 83 mQTL, 10 eQTL, and 2 pQTL signals associated with GC risk. Among these, colocalization evidence was observed for 47 mQTL, 5 eQTL, and 2 pQTL signals. Transcriptomic analysis showed that PCSK6 , YOD1 , and RNF5 exhibited expression changes directionally consistent with their SMR associations with GC risk, whereas CTNNBIP1 showed an inconsistent expression pattern. PCSK6 was supported by mQTL, eQTL, and mQTL-eQTL evidence but lacked colocalization. YOD1 , identified through pQTL-SMR, showed strong colocalization evidence (PPH4 = 0.95). RNF5 was highlighted via eQTL-SMR but lacked colocalization support. CTNNBIP1 was supported by mQTL, eQTL, and mQTL-eQTL evidence and colocalization, with a significant methylation-expression correlation observed in TCGA-STAD. Single-cell RNA-seq revealed that PCSK6 was predominantly expressed in fibroblasts, YOD1 in epithelial cells and mast cells, and RNF5 broadly across fibroblasts, epithelial cells, and selected immune cells. Conclusions This multiomics study prioritized PCSK6 , YOD1 , and RNF5 as ER stress-related candidate genes showing genetic associations with GC risk and directionally consistent expression patterns, with single-cell analysis indicating distinct cell-type-specific expression patterns. These findings offer useful context for future functional and mechanistic investigations of the prioritized candidate genes.

A summary‐data‐based Mendelian randomization (SMR) approach was then employed by integrating gastric cancer (GC) genome‐wide association study (GWAS) data from the FinnGen discovery cohort with quantitative trait loci (QTL) data for DNA methylation (mQTLs), gene expression (eQTLs), and protein abundance (pQTLs). Significant associations were further evaluated in independent GC GWAS datasets from the UK Biobank replication cohorts. Candidate signals were assessed using SMR‐multi, the HEIDI test, and colocalization analysis to prioritize genes with more consistent genetic evidence and reduce the likelihood of linkage disequilibrium‐driven associations. Prioritized genes were further characterized using external transcriptomic analysis in GSE118916 , methylation‐expression correlation analysis in TCGA‐STAD, and single‐cell RNA‐seq analysis in GSE270680 .
