papers.title: Enhancing tumor T-cell antigen prediction using cross-attention-based multimodal representations with hybrid CNN-GLU model.
papers.authors: Raza A, Akbar S, Khan GA, Alghamdi W, Luo X, Xu L.
papers.abstract: Tumor T-cell antigens play a significant role in cancer immunotherapy by enabling the immune system to recognize and eliminate malignant cells. However, existing experimental methods for identifying these antigens are costly, time-consuming, and labor-intensive, highlighting the need for an accurate computational prediction model. In this study, we propose iTTCA-DeepGLU, a deep-learning model for predicting tumor T-cell antigens from peptide sequences. Each peptide sequence was initially transformed into an SMR-based two-dimensional matrix, after which local phase quantization was applied to generate novel intrinsic local descriptors, termed SMR-LPQ features. In parallel, semantic and contextual features were extracted using the pretrained ProtT5 protein language model. The SMR-LPQ and ProtT5 features were then integrated through cross-attention-based fusion to construct a multimodal feature representation. Subsequently, a gradient-boosted decision tree was applied to retain the most informative features. Among the applied classifiers, our hybrid CNN-GLU model demonstrated high predictive performance. The proposed iTTCA-DeepGLU model using Train-DS1 and Train-DS2 datasets achieved accuracies of 95.87% and 96.72%, representing improvements of 8% and 11%, respectively, with corresponding AUC values of 0.97 and 0.98. To evaluate the model's generalizability, it was further assessed using two independent test sets. On the imbalanced Ind-DS1 dataset, the iTTCA-DeepGLU model achieved an accuracy of 90.39%, representing a 14% improvement, with an AUC of 0.94. Similarly, on the balanced Ind-DS2 dataset. iTTCA-DeepGLU attained an accuracy of 95.30%, approximately 2% higher than that of existing tumor T-cell antigen prediction models, with an AUC of 0.92. Overall, iTTCA-DeepGLU demonstrated strong predictive performance and generalization capability, highlighting its potential as a reliable computational tool for identifying tumor T-cell antigens and supporting cancer immunotherapy research.

papers.title: Mapping the Intellectual Architecture of Inflammation-Centered Macrophage Research in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Dual-Database Bibliometric and Scientometric Analysis, 2005-2025.
papers.authors: Chai K, Chen C, Wu K, Zhao X.
papers.abstract: Background Chronic liver inflammation provides a major biological context for hepatocarcinogenesis, and macrophages link innate immune sensing, fibrogenesis, immune suppression and therapeutic resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), Kupffer cells and inflammation-associated myeloid populations have been extensively investigated in HCC; however, the intellectual structure and thematic connectivity of this inflammation-centered research field remain incompletely defined. Objective This study aimed to map the intellectual architecture, evolutionary trajectory and inter-module connectivity of inflammation-centered macrophage research in HCC using bibliometric and scientometric methods. Methods A total of 9218 English-language articles and reviews on macrophage-related HCC from 2005 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus after systematic deduplication. CiteSpace, VOSviewer and bibliometrix were used to perform co-citation clustering, reference historiographic mapping, keyword co-occurrence analysis, publication-volume-adjusted keyword correlation analysis, citation burst detection, journal dual-map overlay and multi-level collaboration profiling. Results Annual publication output increased from 84 articles in 2005 to 1129 in 2025. Co-citation analysis resolved 13 well-defined clusters (modularity Q = 0.744; mean silhouette S = 0.884), and historiographic mapping identified four sequential stages: foundational inflammation and hepatocarcinogenesis, mechanistic expansion of TAM function, immune-regulatory convergence and spatial immunology. Keyword dynamics showed a transition from viral hepatitis, innate immunity, Kupffer cells and fibroinflammatory terminology toward TAM-mediated immune suppression, immunotherapy, single-cell analysis, SPP1-positive macrophage-associated spatial immune barriers and computational precision oncology. After annual publication-volume adjustment, the foundational viral-innate module and the contemporary computational-precision oncology module showed a negative inter-module Pearson correlation (mean r = -0.383), lower than expected under label-permutation and temporal-succession null models (both p Conclusion Macrophage-related HCC research has evolved from inflammation-centered hepatocarcinogenesis toward spatially resolved and computationally assisted immunology. The low-connectivity interfaces identified in this study should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating bibliometric signals rather than as evidence of biological or clinical disconnection or as stand-alone research priorities derived from network structure alone. Their potential translational relevance should be considered alongside published mechanistic and clinical evidence and requires future mechanistic, spatial and prospective clinical validation.

papers.title: Genetic Insights into the Potential Causal Role of LIPA and LTA4H in Vitiligo: A Single-Cell Integrative Analysis.
papers.authors: Zhang Z, Lu H.
papers.abstract: Background Vitiligo is a complex autoimmune skin disorder characterized by the loss of melanocytes, imposing a significant psychosocial and economic burden on affected individuals. Despite the identification of numerous susceptibility loci through GWAS, translating these findings into clinical insights remains challenging as the cell-type-specific causal genes and their regulatory mechanisms are largely unexplored. Identifying these specific drivers is crucial for developing targeted precision therapies. Methods We employed an integrative framework combining single-cell eQTL data and vitiligo GWAS summary statistics to identify cell-type-specific causal genes. Potential causal relationships were evaluated using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and Bayesian colocalization analysis. Functional significance was explored via GO/KEGG enrichment. Finally, the prioritized candidates were validated using PBMC scRNA-seq dataset. Results MR analysis identified several cell-type-specific causal transcripts. Beyond the established HLA-DRB1 in NK recruiting cells (β=1.84, pfdr 0.7) confirmed shared causal variants at these loci. Functional enrichment highlighted lysosomal metabolism and antigen presentation. External validation (GSE231794) confirmed that HLA-DRB1 was significantly up-regulated in patient NK recruiting cells, while LIPA and LTA4H expression were markedly diminished in patients, aligning consistently with our genetic estimates. Conclusion This study provides genetic insights into the potential involvement of LIPA and LTA4H in vitiligo. These findings suggest that a deficiency in these metabolic-immune regulators within specific myeloid subsets may contribute to the disease's pathogenesis, highlighting them as potential targets for further functional investigation and precision intervention. Future studies should focus on in vivo and in vitro functional validation of these genes to further elucidate their precise roles in melanocyte stability and their potential as therapeutic targets for precision intervention.

papers.title: LCK regulates apoptosis and intercellular communication networks in neuroblastoma.
papers.authors: Tafazoli A, Askari N, Jafarinejad Farsangi S.
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma is the most common solid malignancy of childhood with poor prognosis in high-risk patients. The tumor microenvironment, particularly the metastatic bone marrow niche, plays a critical role in disease progression. Lymphocyte-specific protein tyrosine kinase (LCK) is essential for T cell function and implicated in apoptosis induction by anticancer drugs, yet its role in neuroblastoma remains unclear. This study investigated LCK expression changes in neuroblastoma cells following doxorubicin treatment, examined molecular interactions between LCK and doxorubicin, and elucidated LCK's role in the tumor immune microenvironment. Differential LCK expression was analyzed across control, non-metastatic and metastatic neuroblastoma samples using single-cell transcriptomics. CellChat framework mapped immune cell interaction networks. LCK expression was evaluated before and after doxorubicin treatment, and molecular docking assessed direct binding between LCK and doxorubicin. CellChat revealed significantly altered communication between T cells and hematopoietic progenitors in metastatic samples, with increased interactions associated with LCK-expressing cells. Molecular docking suggested a potential interaction between doxorubicin and the LCK kinase domain. Chromosomal localization of LCK at 1p32-35, frequently deleted in aggressive neuroblastomas, underscores its clinical relevance. LCK expression changes were associated with doxorubicin response and apoptosis-related transcriptional changes. These findings suggest LCK as a candidate biomarker for predicting treatment response and a potential target for further investigation in neuroblastoma. Experimental validation is required to establish the functional role of LCK in this context.

papers.title: Microglia-targeted delivery of MCC950 suppresses NLRP3-IL-18-mediated neuroinflammation and retinal injury in retinal vein occlusion.
papers.authors: Xue X, Jiang H, Zhang W, Zhou Y, Li H, Zhou C, Chen Y, Ma W, Gao Y, Ji X, Zhou C, Zhang X.
papers.abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) causes retinal ischemia, macular edema, and vision loss, yet current anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies primarily limit vascular leakage and leave ischemia-driven neuroinflammation insufficiently controlled. Here, we reveal a critical role for microglia-associated NLRP3-IL-18 signaling in amplifying inflammation during early RVO. Bulk retinal RNA sequencing showed broad innate immune activation, whereas single-cell transcriptomic profiling and spatial protein analysis identified prominent inflammasome-related changes in retinal microglia. Constitutive global deletion of Nlrp3 or Il18 attenuated microglial activation and preserved retinal structure and electrophysiological function. To translate this mechanistic insight into a targeted anti-inflammatory strategy, we engineered MG1-functionalized, MCC950-loaded nanoliposomes for microglia-targeted NLRP3 inhibition. MG1 functionalization promoted preferential nanoparticle uptake by activated microglia and suppressed NLRP3-IL-18 signaling more effectively than free MCC950 or non-targeted nanoliposomes. In experimental RVO, a single intravitreal dose administered 6 h after induction alleviated retinal inflammation and edema while preserving retinal electrophysiological responses. These findings establish microglia-associated NLRP3-IL-18 signaling as a therapeutic target in early RVO and support MG1-MCC950 nanoliposomes as a bioactive nanotherapeutic platform for RVO.

papers.title: Biotin-dependent metabolism controls germinal center fate and vaccine-induced antibody diversification.
papers.authors: Hsieh CH, Aala W, Tsai YC, Huang YF, Lin MS, Hwang DY, Shieh DB, Sung HH, Jiang ST, Lin CW, Chen CA, Hughes MW, Chen PC, Shieh CC.
papers.abstract: Nutrient availability shapes antibody responses, yet its role in metabolic checkpoints governing germinal center (GC) B-cell differentiation remains incompletely defined. Using heterozygous (HZ) Slc5a6 M60K mice modeling human loss-of-function mutations in the multivitamin transporter SLC5A6, we found that deficient biotin imports impaired mitochondrial metabolism and restricted preGC-to-dark zone progression after vaccination. Single-cell transcriptomics and RNA velocity revealed disrupted GC trajectories, while B-cell receptor repertoire analysis showed impaired class-switch recombination, somatic hypermutation, and vaccine-induced clonal diversity. Spatial multiplexed imaging showed reduced GL7-high GC-associated B-cell regions. Flow cytometric analyses revealed reduced frequencies of RBD-specific B cells and RBD-specific GL7 + CD95 + GC B cells in HZ mice, with higher frequencies after biotin supplementation. Pseudovirus assays demonstrated impaired neutralization of Wuhan-Hu-1 and Omicron BA.2. Dietary biotin supplementation restored GC-associated differentiation, antibody diversification, and vaccine-induced humoral responses. These findings identify biotin-dependent mitochondrial metabolism as an important checkpoint linking micronutrient availability to GC B-cell differentiation and vaccine responsiveness.

papers.title: Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic characterization of the osteosarcoma microenvironment reveals lineage-specific programs and inflammatory differences associated with metastasis.
papers.authors: Zhou Z, Li Z.
papers.abstract: Background Osteosarcoma is a heterogeneous bone malignancy in which malignant, immune, stromal, and bone-lineage cells form a complex microenvironment. Clinical activity of immune-checkpoint blockade has remained limited in advanced osteosarcoma, motivating cell-type-resolved investigation of the tumor microenvironment while avoiding mechanistic overinterpretation of cross-sectional transcriptomic data. Methods Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from primary osteosarcoma were obtained from GEO (GSE162454; six patients) and analyzed with Scanpy using quality filtering, normalization, highly variable gene selection, principal component analysis, neighborhood graph construction, UMAP, Leiden clustering, and marker-based cell-type annotation. Seven transcriptional programs and ligand-receptor communication scores were evaluated. An independent bulk osteosarcoma cohort with metastatic status and overall survival annotation (GSE21257; n = 53) was used for differential expression, cross-platform comparison, and survival analysis. RT-qPCR was performed in primary human osteoblasts exposed to MG-63 osteosarcoma-conditioned medium. Results After quality control, 44,189 cells with 25,473 detected genes were retained. Leiden clustering resolved 23 clusters annotated into 11 cell types; myeloid cells (34.0%) and osteoblasts (16.6%) were the largest populations. Osteoblasts showed the highest osteogenic program scores, whereas myeloid cells showed the highest inflammatory and immune-evasion scores. Reclustering of osteoblasts, osteocytes, and mesenchymal stromal cells resolved seven stromal subclusters, but pairwise co-expression between representative osteogenic and inflammatory genes was generally weak. Ligand-receptor analysis highlighted MIF-CD74, SPP1-CD44, and SPP1-ITGAV as the strongest scored interactions. In GSE21257, 333 genes differed between metastatic and non-metastatic tumors at FDR In vitro , osteosarcoma-conditioned medium reduced RUNX2 and SP7 and increased SOST and RANKL expression in primary osteoblasts. Conclusion Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses identify lineage-specific osteogenic, inflammatory, and communication programs in osteosarcoma but also demonstrate limited cross-platform generalizability of osteoblast-centered signatures. The RT-qPCR experiment supports an osteoblast transcriptional response to soluble factors from MG-63 cells, but it does not establish a specific immunosuppressive mechanism or prognostic biomarker. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and require independent single-cell, spatial, and functional validation.

papers.title: Rapid Identification of H3N2 Influenza A Virus HA-Targeting Antibody Epitopes Driven by Computational Antibody Similarity Measures.
papers.authors: Zhu Z, Chen Z, Wu J, Han J, Li L, Qian K, Cui Y, Li Z, Ding R, Pang S, Zhang G, Yu C, Chi X.
papers.abstract: Antibodies are important therapeutic agents for the prevention and treatment of influenza, and hemagglutinin (HA) serves as the primary target for the development of therapeutic antibodies. However, the identification of epitopes remains an unmet need in the development of such therapeutic antibodies. This study investigates the characteristics of antibody-HA binding interfaces (i.e., epitopes and paratopes) through a computational analysis of all antibody-HA complexes with nonredundant experimentally determined structures from SAbDab, the largest reported antibody structure data set to date. After experimentally identifying and selecting H3N2 HA-specific binding antibodies, a reference antibody library was established. For anti-H3N2 HA antibodies with unknown structures, epitope grouping was conducted based on competitive binding assays that assess interference with the binding of antibodies from the reference library. Based on the complementary relationship between epitope and paratope structures, we selected the structure-based similarity measure most relevant to epitope convergence. Furthermore, we prioritized the experimental validation of binding interference between candidate antibodies and their most structurally similar reference antibodies. We present an integrated computational and experimental framework. This approach includes the construction of an H3N2-specific reference antibody set, computational modeling of antibodies, measurement of antibody similarity, and is complemented by antibody competition binding assays. The dry-wet iterative protocol presented here yielded accurate assessment of the neutralizing potency and breadth of the previously uncharacterized antibody P2A10. Together, the presented pipeline offers a powerful approach for identifying epitopes on anti-H3N2 HA antibodies and for epitope-targeted antibody discovery, while demonstrating the effectiveness of structural analytics in reducing experimental labor.

papers.title: Evaluating cytokine-based therapeutics in human 3D in vitro immune-containing assembloids.
papers.authors: Maenhoudt N, Lütge M, Obenloch M, Caironi A, Kiratzis M, Jean-Mairet P, Graziano S, Fröbel P, Hüsser T, Yángüez E, Antsiferova M, Filip AM, Müller C, Leclair S, Gasser S, Umaña P, Colombetti S, Cremasco F, Calabro S.
papers.abstract: Introduction Cancer immunotherapies require accurate preclinical models that recapitulate the complex cellular interactions within the human tumor microenvironment. While patient-derived organoids have emerged as powerful tools for cancer research, standard cultures lack the stromal and immune compartments necessary to evaluate immunotherapeutic mechanisms. This limitation hampers the development of next-generation targeted cytokine therapies. Methods We applied a 3D immune-containing colorectal cancer assembloid platform integrating patient-derived organoids, cancer-associated fibroblasts and allogeneic peripheral blood mononuclear cells within a collagen matrix. We characterized cellular responses to interferon-gamma (IFNg) and engineered IFNg receptor agonists targeted to fibroblast activation protein (FAP) through single-cell transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry, cytokine profiling, and functional T-cell migration assays. Results The assembloid model successfully recapitulated key features of IFNg signaling, including tissue growth suppression, enhanced chemokine secretion (CXCL10), and CD8 + T-cell recruitment. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that fibroblasts were the most responsive cell population, undergoing a phenotypic transition from myofibroblasts toward antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs), characterized by robust upregulation of MHC class II genes. FAP-targeted IFNg molecules exhibited attenuated activity compared to recombinant IFNg, successfully avoiding upregulation of the severe immunosuppressive checkpoint molecule PD-L1. Discussion This 3D assembloid model provides a physiologically relevant platform for dissecting complex tumor-immune interactions and optimizing targeted immunotherapies. This approach enables the study of epithelial-stromal-immune crosstalk in cancer and offers a robust preclinical framework for screening and mechanistically validating next-generation targeted cytokine therapies.

papers.title: Gut bacterial lauroyl tryptamine reduces GPR183-associated inflammatory responses in human macrophages and T cells in vitro .
papers.authors: Lezzerini M, Spek V, Fung ICN, Müller MJ, Kubelka A, Sieber S, de Jonge WJ, Li Yim AYF, Te Velde AA, Zhang J.
papers.abstract: Introduction Recent research has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in producing bioactive metabolites that interact with G-protein coupled receptors (GPRs) and influence immune responses. Lauroyl tryptamine (LT), a metabolite produced by Agathobacter rectalis (formerly Eubacterium rectale ), has been reported to antagonize GPR183, a receptor implicated in inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD). LT inhibits the binding of GPR183 with its natural ligands 7a,25-dihydroxycholesterol (OHC). Methods Here, we analyzed the GPR183 gene expression in intestinal tissues from IBD patients and non-IBD controls, as well as our previous single-cell transcriptomic dataset to identify key GPR183-expressing cells. We then use in vitro THP-1 derived macrophage and Jurkat T cell culture to test the effects of LT on inflammatory responses. Results and discussion The GPR183 gene expression is elevated specifically in colonic and rectal tissues of ulcerative colitis patients, but not in Crohn's disease or ileal tissue. By analyzing single-cell transcriptomic dataset, we identified monocytes/macrophages, T cells, B cells, and innate lymphoid cells as key GPR183 -expressing populations in human intestine. Using cell culture models, we demonstrated that LT modulates inflammatory pathways. In LPS-stimulated macrophages, OHC increased transcription of pro-inflammatory genes IL6, TNFA , and IL1B , which are reduced by LT. In activated Jurkat T cells, LT slightly decreased the OHC-mediated increase in the transcription of IL2. These findings support the hypothesis that LT, a known GPR183 antagonist, could modulate GPR183-associated inflammation in human macrophages and T cells in a context- and cell type-dependent manner, offering potential mechanistic insights into bioactive metabolite-mediated host-microbiota interactions in human intestine.

papers.title: An oral-origin Streptococcus salivarius associated with schizophrenia reshapes intestinal T-cell immunity and promotes IL-17A-dominated inflammation.
papers.authors: Kang Y, Fan Y, Ma Q, Yu L, Liu J, Liu Y, Zhou Z, Zhao H, Yang Z, Xun Y, Jia M, Zhao B, Ma X, Wang W, Guo Y.
papers.abstract: Background Emerging evidence suggests that oral microbial dysbiosis contributes to neuropsychiatric disorders through microbiome-immune interactions. We previously identified an oral-origin Streptococcus salivarius enriched in individuals with schizophrenia (SCZ) and demonstrated its ability to become enriched in the intestine after oral administration. However, whether this disease-associated bacterium remodels host adaptive immunity remains unclear. Here, we investigated the effects of S. salivarius on intestinal CD4 + T-cell homeostasis and inflammatory responses. Methods Male C57BL/6 mice were orally administered S. salivarius for 14 days with or without prior antibiotic-mediated depletion of resident microbiota. Intestinal enrichment of S. salivarius was confirmed by quantitative PCR. Colonic lamina propria mononuclear cells (LPMCs) and mesenteric lymph node (MLN) cells were analyzed using single-cell RNA sequencing and flow cytometry to characterize CD4 + T cell responses. Cytokine levels in colon tissues and serum were quantified by ELISA. Results Single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrated that intestinal enrichment of S. salivarius altered Treg-associated transcriptional programs, with reduced Treg-stability signatures and increased Type-17-associated features. Flow cytometry confirmed increased Th17 cells, reduced Treg frequencies, and disruption of intestinal Th17/Treg homeostasis. Similar immune alternations were observed in MLNs, indicating extension of gut-associated immune remodeling beyond the intestinal mucosa. S. salivarius exposure was further associated with selective IL-17A in colonic tissues and serum, whereas IL-6, IL-1β, IL-10, and TGF-β remained largely unchanged. Comparable immune changes were observed in both antibiotic-pretreated and conventional SPF mice, indicating that these immunological effects were not restricted to microbiota-depletion condition. Discussion These findings identify an SCZ-associated oral-origin S. salivarius as a modulator of intestinal adaptive immunity. Intestinal enrichment of S. salivarius was associated with coordinated remodeling of Treg-associated transcriptional programs, Th17-biased immune polarization, and an IL-17A-dominated inflammatory response, Together, these results define an intestinal immune mechanism through which a disease-associated oral bacterium may contribute to oral-gut immune interactions and provide experimental support for one immunological component of the oral-gut-brain axis relevant to schizophrenia.

papers.title: Camel milk concerning erythrocytic immune-related gene expression in Escherichia coli -challenged broilers.
papers.authors: Arain U, Rajput N, Arain M, Jahejo AR, Lee Y, Zhang G.
papers.abstract: Background Chicken erythrocytes play a role in immunity, yet the function of erythrocyte-related immune genes during Escherichia coli ( E. coli ) infection remains underexplored. This study investigated the effects of camel milk powder supplementation on growth performance and erythrocyte-specific immune gene expression in E. coli -challenged broiler chickens. Methods A total of 240 one-day-old broiler chickens were randomly assigned to four groups with three replicates (20 Chickens per replicate): Control (Basal diet + PBS), Infected ( E. coli challenged), T1 ( E. coli + 5 g/kg camel milk), and T2 ( E. coli + 10 g/kg camel milk). Performance metrics, organ weights, intestinal and hepatic histomorphology, hematological parameters, and viable E. coli counts in blood and cecum were assessed. Bioinformatics analysis of microarray data (GPL8764) guided the selection of key immune genes. Quantitative real-time PCR was performed on purified erythrocytes to evaluate immune gene expression. Results Feed intake, weight gain, and FCR were significantly ( p Conclusion The camel milk supplementation at 5 g/kg, effectively mitigated the negative impacts of E. coli infection by enhancing growth performance, reducing bacterial load, and modulating immune responses.

papers.title: YAP-dependent transcriptional responses in tenocytes under cyclic tensile loading: a conditional knockout RNA-sequencing study.
papers.authors: Xing X, Piacentini A, Suzuki Y, Sanchez LA, Mendias C, Rodeo SA.
papers.abstract: Background Tendon injuries are prevalent across various populations and significantly impair quality of life, presenting substantial healthcare challenges. Purpose This study aimed to characterize Yes-associated protein (YAP) -dependent transcriptional responses in tenocytes under cyclic tensile loading, using a conditional YAP knockout approach combined with RNA sequencing. Given that tenocytes in vivo are continuously exposed to mechanical loading, this design was intended to identify genes whose regulation by YAP becomes critical under mechanical challenge. Methods Employing conditional gene knockout techniques with RosaCreERT2 YAP-floxed mice and mechanical loading protocols, alongside RNA sequencing and advanced bioinformatics analyses. Results We identified 54 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in tenocytes after YAP knockout, including six upregulated and 48 downregulated genes. Notably, upregulated genes included Gzmc and Gm28151, while downregulated genes included Car3 and Rgs2. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses highlighted significant pathways, such as the PPAR signaling pathway, emphasizing their relevance in tendon pathophysiology. Furthermore, CIBERSORTx analysis revealed significant differences in immune cell infiltration, particularly in Treg and CD4 naive T cells, suggesting a link between YAP-dependent pathways and immune responses in tendon healing. Drug prediction analyses identified several small molecules interacting with hub genes, including LTC4S and CXCL13, indicating potential pharmacological targets for therapeutic intervention. Conclusion Despite limitations such as a lack of in vivo validation and small sample size, this research underscores the pivotal role of YAP in tenocyte mechanotransduction and identifies key DEGs and pathways that may inform future therapeutic strategies for tendon injuries. Future studies should focus on the in-vivo implications of these findings and explore the potential for immune modulation and pharmacological interventions in tendon repair.

papers.title: Intelligence-enabled smart inhalable biomaterials for chronic inflammatory airway diseases: integrating responsive carrier engineering, lung-on-chip validation, and patient-specific pulmonary modeling.
papers.authors: Fan Q, Li Z, Sun Y, Liu Y, Chen H.
papers.abstract: Chronic inflammatory airway diseases, particularly asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), are commonly treated by inhalation, yet the nominal dose placed in an inhaler often differs substantially from the dose that reaches diseased airway regions, crosses mucus, enters target cells, and remains pharmacologically active. Airway narrowing, heterogeneous ventilation, mucus plugging, impaired mucociliary clearance, oxidative and proteolytic stress, epithelial barrier dysfunction, inflammatory-cell diversity, device characteristics, and patient-specific inhalation maneuvers jointly shape therapeutic exposure. Smart inhalable biomaterials can be designed to address some of these barriers by controlling transport, retention, activation, or release, but many systems are still optimized primarily at the nanoparticle level and evaluated in static models that do not capture realistic aerosol performance or patient-specific deposition. This review develops an intelligence-enabled bioengineering framework linking disease-informed material design with machine-learning-assisted formulation optimization, formulation-device-patient coupling, lung-on-chip validation, and patient-specific pulmonary modeling. Within this framework, airway features such as mucus architecture, redox gradients, protease activity, epithelial permeability, immune-cell state, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and regional airflow are considered measurable variables that can inform material design and evaluation. The material platforms considered include mucus-penetrating and mucoadhesive carriers, responsive materials, transformable nano-in-micro systems, polymeric and lipid nanoparticles, biomimetic carriers, extracellular vesicles, and systems for pulmonary delivery of nucleic acids and biologics. Their development is considered alongside structured experimental design, machine learning, active learning, mechanistic aerosol modeling, physics-informed surrogates, multi-objective optimization, and uncertainty analysis. Lung-on-chip systems provide human-relevant settings in which deposited dose, mucus transport, barrier function, immune responses, and repeated-exposure effects can be examined under air-liquid-interface and breathing-like conditions. Patient-specific computational fluid dynamics and reduced-order models can complement these platforms by predicting regional deposition, whereas the term digital twin should be reserved for longitudinally updated, uncertainty-aware models linked to actionable decisions. Together, these approaches support a closed-loop design-delivery-validation strategy in which material performance, aerosol behavior, biological response, and patient-specific deposition are evaluated as connected rather than separate development problems.

papers.title: BKPyVN-associated macrophage subpopulations and diagnostic biomarker identification - combine machine learning with single-cell analysis.
papers.authors: Xu S, Zhao G, He Y, Mo J, Huang G.
papers.abstract: Background As pivotal effector cells of innate immunity, macrophages may play a critical role in immune regulation and fibrotic remodeling in BK polyomavirus nephropathy (BKPyVN) following kidney transplantation. However, their subpopulation heterogeneity, molecular characteristics, and functional mechanisms remain poorly understood. Methods We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data from BKPyVN and stable transplant kidney (STK) biopsies. Pseudotime trajectory, CellChat, and high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA) were used to characterize BKPyVN-associated macrophages (BKPyVN-Mac) and identify related gene modules. Characteristic genes from these modules were used to construct diagnostic models from an integrated renal allograft microarray dataset, and nine machine-learning algorithms were compared. Key genes were validated by RT-qPCR and immunohistochemistry in human biopsies and by time-course transcript and protein analyses in a persistent mouse polyomavirus (MPyV) infection model. Results BKPyVN-Mac occupied a disease-associated macrophage state and may serve as a central communication hub within the allograft microenvironment. The support vector machine model exhibited the best diagnostic performance, with the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC = 0.923). ATF4 and MCL1 were identified as key feature genes, and their upregulation was confirmed in human BKPyVN biopsies and, through their mouse orthologs Atf4 and Mcl1, in the persistent MPyV infection model. Functional analysis suggested that these genes are associated with inflammation, fibrotic remodeling, and metabolic regulation. Conclusion This study characterizes the molecular phenotype and regulatory network of a BKPyVN-Mac subpopulation, providing new insights into BKPyVN pathophysiology and identifying candidate biomarkers for clinical diagnosis.

papers.title: Long-term high-fat diet and long-term high-refined-carbohydrate diet induce alterations in the splenic TCRβ CDR3 repertoire and peripheral multi-compartmental immune parameters in mice.
papers.authors: Wang J, Gao S, Cai Y, Zhang Y, Weng W, Han P, Sun H.
papers.abstract: Background High-fat diet (HFD) and high-refined carbohydrate diet (HRCD) are closely associated with elevated risks of chronic inflammation, autoimmune diseases, and infectious diseases. However, the molecular alterations of the immune system following long-term intervention with these two diets remain unclear. Methods 3-month-old young male mice were used as the animal model and received long-term intervention with HFD or HRCD until 14 months of age. Comparative analyses were performed on the pathological characteristics of immune organs, immune cell subsets, serum proteomics, and TCRβ CDR3 repertoire characteristics detected by next-generation sequencing. Results Both dietary interventions led to increased body weight and caused similar splenic pathological damage in mice. Their effects on the immune system were dominated by peripheral alterations with mild central changes. Meanwhile, both diets led to increased clonal concentration, decreased uniformity, depletion of low-frequency clones, and expansion of mid-frequency clones in the splenic TCRβ CDR3 repertoire while also identifying a clonotype CSSRAGGLNSDYTF whose abundance in both the thymus and spleen was significantly higher in the HFD and HRCD groups than in the Control group. In contrast, the specific mechanisms underlying immune regulation differed significantly between the two diets. HFD significantly upregulated the levels of serum IL-6, IL-10, TNF-α and FAS, altered the proportion of splenic T cell subsets, and strongly affected splenic TRBJ gene usage and CDR3 length distribution. HRCD predominantly increased IL-17A levels and the proportion of DCs. Conclusion This study preliminarily demonstrates that HFD and HRCD can induce similar pathological phenotypes but distinct molecular immune mechanisms, both showing more pronounced alterations in the spleen than in the thymus under the parameters examined.

papers.title: B-cell receptor repertoire remodeling in Kawasaki disease is associated with clonal expansion and distinct repertoire features in coronary artery lesions.
papers.authors: Xu Y, Lin X, Chen Y, Zhang X, Ma L, Yao X, Li J.
papers.abstract: Background Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute systemic vasculitis in children, but the characteristics of the B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire during acute disease and their association with coronary artery lesions (CALs) remain poorly understood. Methods High-throughput sequencing of BCR heavy-chain (BCR-H) CDR3 regions was performed in 22 children, including 9 healthy controls and 13 patients with KD, of whom 9 had no CAL and 4 had CAL. Repertoire diversity, clonal expansion, immunoglobulin isotype distribution, V-J gene usage, CDR3 characteristics, and inter-individual and cross-isotype repertoire sharing were systematically evaluated. Results KD exhibited reduced BCR repertoire diversity, with a significant decrease in IgM diversity. The repertoire showed increased contributions of high-frequency and hyperexpanded clonotypes, with the most pronounced expansion in patients with CAL. IgM displayed the strongest clonal remodeling, characterized by reduced low-frequency and increased highly abundant clonotypes. KD also showed selective alterations in IGHV usage and V-J gene pairing. CAL was associated with increased IGHA usage and changes in CDR3 amino acid composition. Substantial inter-individual CDR3 sharing was observed among KD patients, and 20 recurrent clonotypes absent from healthy controls were identified as candidate KD-associated sequences. Cross-isotype CDR3 sharing also tended to be higher in KD, particularly among patients with CAL. Conclusions Acute KD is characterized by substantial BCR repertoire remodeling, marked by selective IgM clonal expansion, repertoire convergence, and CAL-associated IgA-biased remodeling. These findings provide new insights into humoral immune dysregulation in KD and identify candidate B-cell clonotypes for further investigation of disease pathogenesis and coronary involvement.

papers.title: Machine-learning-assisted integration of single-cell and bulk transcriptomics characterizes glioblastoma ecosystem states and immune-associated programs.
papers.authors: Cao J, Cheng H, Wang Y, Zhao B, Wang Y, Jiang X.
papers.abstract: Background Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by marked malignant-cell plasticity and a complex tumor ecosystem composed of heterogeneous malignant and microenvironmental cell populations. We integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to characterize reproducible GBM cell and ecosystem-associated states, evaluate cross-platform concordance, and examine immune-associated transcriptional programs while distinguishing descriptive associations from mechanistic inference. Methods The deposited Smart-seq2 (7,930 cells) and 10x (16,201 cells) expression matrices from GSE131928/SCP393 were analyzed on their verified expression scales. Official annotations and malignant-state modules were audited, four broad malignant states were recomputed, and a tumor-held-out machine-learning label-transfer framework was applied to the 10x dataset. Public TCGA-GBM RNA-seq data were used to evaluate state- and microenvironment-associated transcriptional programs and to perform nested prediction benchmarking. Selected ecosystem-associated genes were additionally examined by RT-qPCR in glioma cell lines and normal human astrocytes. Results Among Smart-seq2 cells, 6,576 malignant cells had valid state scores, whereas 287 alias-affected records were excluded from state-score denominators. The machine-learning label-transfer model achieved an out-of-fold accuracy of 0.998, and malignant-state fractions showed moderate-to-strong concordance across six shared tumor labels. At the tumor-label level, MES-like fraction was not significantly associated with macrophage fraction (Spearman rho = 0.171, P = 0.395), indicating that ecosystem-level transcriptional association should not be interpreted as a simple directional immune-to-state mechanism. In TCGA-GBM, MES and myeloid-associated programs correlated with immune and stromal expression signatures, whereas survival and 12-month prediction performance remained modest and specification-sensitive. RT-qPCR further demonstrated increased STAT3, CHI3L1, SPP1, and VEGFA expression in glioma cell lines relative to normal human astrocytes. Conclusion Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis supports reproducible characterization of malignant-cell heterogeneity and immune-associated ecosystem features in IDH-wildtype GBM. Machine-learning-assisted cross-platform analysis provides a reproducible framework for evaluating tumor ecosystem-associated states, while the observed immune-mesenchymal associations remain descriptive rather than causal. Experimental RT-qPCR provides expression-level support for selected ecosystem-associated genes and highlights testable hypotheses for future functional and spatial studies.

papers.title: Admission immune-inflammatory biomarker profiles for trauma severity stratification: an externally validated machine learning study.
papers.authors: Dai X, Zhang L, Wu Z, Xu H, Chen B, Zhou Y, Xiao Y, Wu Y, Xiang S, He J, Bao J, Huang Y.
papers.abstract: Background Traumatic injury induces rapid systemic immune-inflammatory alterations, but whether routinely measurable admission biomarkers can provide an early biological estimate of anatomical injury burden remains uncertain. This study aimed to characterize trauma-associated immune-inflammatory profiles across trauma severity levels defined by injury severity score (ISS) and evaluate their combined value for early severity stratification. Methods This two-center retrospective study included healthy participants as a physiological reference group, non-trauma acute-care patients as a clinically relevant comparator, and trauma patients classified as mild (ISS 25). Nineteen admission laboratory biomarkers and demographic variables were evaluated in a development cohort of 775 participants and an independent external validation cohort of 349 participants. Multinomial least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used to identify severity-associated biomarkers. Ten classifiers were compared on the same predefined trauma-only development split, and the selected model was evaluated in an independent external trauma cohort. Results A 10-feature panel was retained following feature selection and collectively defined an immune-inflammatory profile associated with increasing trauma severity. Increasing injury burden was associated with heterogeneous and partly nonlinear inflammatory and hematologic alterations, including changes in neutrophil-related indices, lymphocyte-related measures, and albumin. The multinomial logistic regression model achieved the best overall performance, with an accuracy of 0.941 and 0.973 in the internal holdout and external validation cohorts, respectively, with an external macro-AUC of 0.993. Model interpretation consistently identified neutrophil count and RDW-CV as major contributors to severity stratification. Conclusion Admission-stage blood biomarkers capture reproducible immune-inflammatory alterations associated with increasing anatomical injury severity. Their combined analysis may provide a complementary approach for early biological assessment of injury burden and supports further investigation of clinically accessible biomarkers of trauma-associated immune-inflammatory dysregulation.

papers.title: An AI-derived inflammation-metabolism ecosystem signature reveals ATP2A2 as a microenvironment-remodeling driver of immune evasion in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Hu X, Zhang G, Zhang Y, Zhao Y, Zhou F, Li G.
papers.abstract: Background Chronic inflammation and metabolic dysregulation are increasingly recognized as interconnected drivers of tumorigenesis and immune evasion, yet their combined prognostic and mechanistic relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains poorly defined. Methods A curated 117-gene set representing systemic inflammation-metabolism dysregulation was obtained from MSigDB. Core prognostic genes were identified through differential expression analysis and univariate Cox regression. Using TCGA-LUAD as the training cohort and six independent GEO cohorts for external validation, 101 machine learning algorithm combinations were systematically evaluated to construct a robust prognostic model. Model performance was assessed by C-index, time-dependent ROC, and PCA. Immune characteristics were analyzed using TCIA, ESTIMATE, and TIMER-based deconvolution. ATP2A2, identified as the gene most strongly correlated with risk score, underwent multi-cohort transcriptomic and immunohistochemical validation, in vitro functional characterization, and mechanistic investigation via IOBR-integrated immune profiling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and multiplex immunofluorescence provided cellular-resolution verification of microenvironmental associations. Results The RSF + SuperPC model achieved optimal performance and effectively stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly divergent survival across all seven cohorts. High-risk tumors showed reduced immune/stromal infiltration and elevated tumor purity. ATP2A2 was consistently overexpressed in tumor tissue, correlated with poor differentiation, advanced stage, and shorter survival, and predicted immunotherapy resistance. Mechanistically, high ATP2A2 expression was associated with suppressed immune cell infiltration, attenuated chemokine signaling, impaired cancer-immunity cycle activity, and an "immune-desert" phenotype confirmed by single-cell and spatial analyses. Conclusion This study establishes a validated inflammation-metabolism-based prognostic signature in LUAD and identifies ATP2A2 as a key driver linking tumor aggressiveness to immunosuppressive microenvironment remodeling, positioning it as a promising prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target for overcoming immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Acrolein target-linked toxicological perturbation and tumor-immune microenvironment heterogeneity in colorectal cancer.
papers.authors: Cheng G, Shan L, Shi W, Liu X, Tao X, Han J.
papers.abstract: Background Acrolein is a highly reactive aldehyde generated endogenously during lipid peroxidation and encountered through environmental and dietary exposures. Although acrolein has established electrophilic, genotoxic, and oxidative-stress effects, the extent to which acrolein-linked gene perturbation is represented in colorectal cancer (CRC) transcriptomes and relates to tumor immune-stromal heterogeneity remains incompletely characterized. Methods We integrated direct human acrolein target evidence from the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) with TCGA-COAD/READ bulk RNA-sequencing profiles and a single-cell RNA-sequencing subset from GSE231559. The CTD curation yielded 179 unique direct human targets. Bulk analyses included 624 primary-tumor and 51 solid-tissue normal profiles. Single-cell analyses included six tumor and three normal libraries, yielding 24,128 retained cells assigned to eight broad marker-supported compartments. Target dysregulation burden, immune-stromal expression programs, and library-aware single-cell target localization were evaluated as transcriptomic summaries. In addition, RT-qPCR was performed in HCT 116 colorectal carcinoma cells to experimentally evaluate four measurable CTD targets (NFKBIA, GSTP1, VIM, and GPX4) after acrolein exposure. Results The bulk tumor-normal analysis identified 5,594 differentially expressed genes at FDR p = 3.62e-42). Within primary tumors, target burden correlated negatively with T-cell and endothelial programs (rho = -0.27 for each), myeloid (rho = -0.20), fibroblast-ECM (rho = -0.19), and antigen-presentation programs (rho = -0.20), and positively with cell cycle (rho = 0.20). In single-cell data, descriptive mean target scores were highest in myeloid cells (0.455), fibroblasts (0.424), and endothelial cells (0.344). Cross-scale effects for 154 shared targets showed modest concordance (rho = 0.31, p = 6.95e-05). RT-qPCR showed vehicle-normalized relative expression of 2.18 ± 0.14 for NFKBIA, 1.83 ± 0.13 for GSTP1, 1.57 ± 0.15 for VIM, and 0.71 ± 0.09 for GPX4 after acrolein exposure (mean ± SD of three biological replicates). Conclusions Acrolein target-linked expression perturbation is detectable in CRC and is associated with immune-stromal heterogeneity across bulk and single-cell transcriptomic scales. RT-qPCR provides targeted experimental support for acrolein-responsive expression changes in NFKBIA, GSTP1, VIM, and GPX4 in HCT 116 cells. These findings support a toxicogenomic framework for hypothesis generation but do not measure acrolein exposure in patients, establish causal toxicological effects in human tumors, or demonstrate a specific intercellular signaling mechanism. Additional mechanistic, protein/adduct, dose-response, and independent-cohort validation will be required to determine the biological significance of the observed associations.

papers.title: Neutrophil recruitment and function mediate sexual dimorphism in experimental periodontitis.
papers.authors: Martin K, Maglaras V, Mianecki MJ, Sheikh A, Gupta R, Dabaja RS, Saleh MHA, Decker AM, Decker JT.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that has been shown to have biological sex-based differences with respect to disease prevalence and severity. Understanding the mechanisms behind this difference may highlight potential adjunctive therapies for periodontal disease that could address differences in disease progression between males and females. Our objective was to examine clinical and immunological differences between male and female mice in periodontal disease progression using the ligature-induced periodontitis model. Periodontitis was induced in male and female C57BL/6J mice for 7 or 21 days, at which point maxillae were characterized for bone loss by microCT or immune infiltrate by flow cytometry. Ligature-induced periodontitis led to alveolar bone loss at both 7 and 21 days in both female and male mice. Males and females had similar linear bone loss 7 days post-ligature placement, while male mice had significantly more linear bone loss by day 21. Male mice had significantly more immune cells in their maxillae 7 days post-ligature placement compared to female mice ( p < 0.05). Both male and female mice showed a shift in immune populations towards neutrophils, with no significant difference between males and females. Neutrophil counts were elevated in male mice on day 7 but not day 21, while female mice did not have any statistically significant changes in neutrophil counts. Neutrophil depletion using a Ly6G antibody limited bone loss in male but not female mice relative to isotype antibody-treated controls. Analysis of single-cell sequencing data from human patients with periodontitis showed that, similar to males in our mouse model, male patients with periodontitis showed enrichment for CXCR4 expression with low CD62L (SELL). Padi4 knockout in male and female mice had decreased bone loss at 21 days post-ligature compared with WTs and still displayed sexual dimorphism. Together, these data suggest a mechanistic role for neutrophil inflammation in sexual dimorphism in periodontitis.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers persistent hepatic immunometabolic remodeling following SARS-CoV-2 infection in obese hosts.
papers.authors: Qian W, Wei X, Park SJ, Garcia Diaz J, Comlekoglu T, Yu J, Sun J, Hahn YS.
papers.abstract: SARS-CoV-2 infection affects multiple organs, and chronic post-viral tissue injury is often associated with persistent immune dysregulation. Obesity and related metabolic disorders are major risk factors for severe COVID-19 and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 infection (PASC), including liver dysfunction. To define hepatic responses during post-acute infection, we studied lean and diet-induced obese mice at 7 and 28 days following infection with mouse-adapted SARS-CoV-2. Compared with lean mice, obese mice exhibited persistent lung inflammation and fibrosis, along with liver injury characterized by increased lipid accumulation, cellular apoptosis, and metabolic dysfunction. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed obesity-associated alterations in hepatic immune and metabolic programs during post-acute infection. In particular, hepatic macrophages in obese mice showed sustained inflammatory and metabolic transcriptional alterations, while hepatocytes displayed altered programs associated with gluconeogenesis and lipid metabolism. Endothelial cells also exhibited persistent transcriptional changes linked to immune activation and prothrombotic pathways. These alterations remained evident at 28 days post-infection, suggesting incomplete restoration of immune and metabolic homeostasis in obese liver. Collectively, our findings reveal persistent obesity-associated hepatic immunometabolic remodeling following SARS-CoV-2 infection and identify cellular and molecular programs that may contribute to post-acute liver sequelae in metabolically compromised hosts.

papers.title: Decoding molecular heterogeneity in lupus nephritis: integrating single-cell and spatial multi-omics for endotype-driven precision therapeutics.
papers.authors: Zhou J, Xiao W, Jian H.
papers.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) develops in 40-60% of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and remains the leading cause of renal morbidity and progression to end-stage renal disease (ESRD). While the upstream immunological events initiating LN-including loss of self-tolerance, pathogenic autoantibody production, glomerular immune complex deposition, and type I interferon (IFN) activation-are broadly shared, accumulating evidence demonstrates that these convergent triggers give rise to molecularly heterogeneous tissue injury programs at the renal level. This fundamental divergence provides a mechanistic explanation for the inconsistent therapeutic responses observed with standardized immunosuppressive protocols. Advances in single-cell transcriptomics, spatial gene expression mapping, CITE-seq, and cross-platform multi-omic integration have deconvolved this heterogeneity into at least five recognizable tissue-level injury programs: (i) an IFN-γ-polarized macrophage-tubular epithelial cell co-activation circuit, (ii) a Tfh-B cell ectopic germinal center pathway, (iii) a neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-driven inflammatory cascade, (iv) a podocyte-autonomous injury program, and (v) a TREM2+ macrophage-orchestrated fibrotic program. Concurrently, multiplexed urinary biomarker platforms are under development as non-invasive surrogates for tissue-level pathogenic activity. This review synthesizes current understanding of disease mechanisms, molecular profiling evidence, biomarker candidates, and mechanism-directed therapies corresponding to each tissue injury program. We map existing and investigational agents-including anifrolumab, obinutuzumab, voclosporin, CAR-T cell therapy, and complement inhibitors-to their mechanistic targets and delineate the design requirements for prospective biomarker-stratified trials essential to validating molecularly guided treatment selection.

papers.authors: Yi S, Chen Q, Wu J, Hou H, Chen H, Zhang W, Zhu K, Liu B, Liang P, Zhang S, Yang D.
papers.abstract: Background Early-onset gastric cancer (EOGC) represents a clinically and biologically distinct subtype of gastric cancer characterized by unique molecular features. However, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study aimed to identify EOGC-associated hub genes using an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning framework. Methods Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between EOGC and late-onset gastric cancer (LOGC) were analyzed using functional enrichment, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and random forest algorithms. Immune infiltration was characterized using CIBERSORT. Candidate hub genes were validated using an independent external cohort, clinical specimens, single-cell transcriptomic datasets, and in vitro functional assays. A five-gene logistic regression model was established and evaluated using ROC-AUC, calibration analysis, and bootstrap resampling. Results Transcriptomic analysis identified 227 DEGs, and WGCNA identified seven co-expression modules, with the green module showing the strongest association with EOGC. Machine learning identified five hub genes: CCR7, CD1D, PTGER2, PIK3CG, and EBI3. The combined model showed good discriminatory performance in the training, internal validation, and independent external validation cohorts (AUC = 0.909, 0.859, and 0.802, respectively). Bootstrap resampling yielded AUC estimates of 0.908, 0.852, and 0.789, respectively, supporting model stability. All five genes showed higher expression in EOGC and were validated at the mRNA and protein levels. Immune profiling and single-cell analysis revealed an immune-associated molecular phenotype and distinct expression patterns across immune cell subsets. Silencing the hub genes suppressed gastric cancer cell proliferation and migration in vitro . Conclusion We identified five EOGC-associated hub genes and revealed an immune-associated molecular landscape. The five-gene model represents an EOGC-associated molecular signature distinguishing EOGC from LOGC rather than a stand-alone clinical diagnostic tool. These findings provide insights into the molecular and immune biology of EOGC and may inform future studies of molecular stratification and treatment-related outcomes.

papers.title: Identification of SLC15A3 as a shared prognostic biomarker for AML and COVID-19 via integrative bioinformatics, machine learning and Mendelian randomization.
papers.authors: Liu M, Zhu J, Li H.
papers.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is a lethal hematological malignancy with poor overall prognosis.COVID-19 co-infection further complicates clinical management and worsens survival outcomes of AML patients, highlighting the need to explore the molecular interplay between the two diseases. In this study, we initially screened 109 common differentially expressed genes shared by AML and COVID-19 from public transcriptomic datasets, which were closely involved in tumor progression and viral pathogenesis. We further characterized their biological functions, constructed protein interaction and TF-miRNA regulatory networks, and established an AML prognostic model to evaluate the tumor immune microenvironment. Combining survival analysis, clinical correlation, immune infiltration assessment and m 6 A modification analysis, SLC15A3 was preliminarily screened as a candidate prognostic gene for AML. Subsequent weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning (ML) and Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses further identified SLC15A3 as a promising prognostic biomarker for AML. Finally, RT-qPCR and Western blotting assays verified its aberrant expression in AML cells. Consistent with bioinformatic prediction, SLC15A3 serves as a shared candidate biomarker for AML and COVID-19,although its mechanistic role linking AML and SARS-CoV-2-related inflammation requires further functional validation.

papers.title: Metabolic control of methylation landscapes in cancer growth and plasticity: targeting the epigenetic-metabolic axis with natural compounds and emerging therapies.
papers.authors: Liu Q, Yu Y, Li W, Chen X, Shi Z, Li G, Wei S, Luo Z.
papers.abstract: Cancer cell plasticity enables tumor cells to dynamically transition between diverse phenotypic states, including epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity stemness, dormancy, lineage switching, immune evasion, and therapy-resistant phenotypes. Although metabolic reprogramming and epigenetic regulation have each been recognized as hallmarks of cancer, the mechanistic framework linking metabolic adaptation to dynamic cell-state transitions remains incompletely understood. In this Review, we propose that methylation serves as a major mechanistic interface through which metabolic rewiring can influence adaptive cancer cell plasticity. We discuss how one-carbon metabolism regulates the availability of the universal methyl donor S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), thereby influencing DNA methylation, histone methylation, and multiple forms of RNA methylation, with N6-methyladenosine (m 6 A) representing the principal RNA modification discussed in this review. Rather than responding uniformly to metabolic change, these methylation systems represent distinct but metabolically connected regulatory layers that share dependence on one-carbon metabolism while differing in their biochemical sensitivities and regulatory outputs. Net methylation states, however, are also shaped by metabolically constrained demethylation, including α-ketoglutarate-, oxygen-, Fe 2+ -, and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD)-dependent eraser pathways. Together, these metabolically responsive writing and erasing processes influence transcriptional stability, chromatin accessibility, and post-transcriptional regulation during reversible cell-state transitions. We further examine how environmental and therapeutic stresses, including hypoxia, nutrient limitation, immune surveillance, and anticancer therapy, reshape methylation programs through metabolic adaptation, and how such remodeling may support phenotypic flexibility and survival under selective pressure. Building upon these advances, we propose the concept of the adaptive methylation landscape, a perturbation-responsive, state-associated, and potentially reversible distribution of methylation states that contributes to shaping the spectrum of cellular states accessible during tumor evolution. Finally, we discuss emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the metabolic-methylation axis and highlight how single-cell multi-omics, spatial epigenomics, functional epigenome editing, and AI may enable dynamic mapping of adaptive methylation landscapes. We propose that cancer cell plasticity is not merely a genetic phenomenon but can also be shaped by metabolically responsive methylation programs, providing a testable conceptual framework for future precision epigenetic therapies.

Methionine, serine, glycine, and folate support one-carbon metabolism and regulate intracellular S-adenosylmethionine/S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAM/SAH) balance, thereby constraining SAM-dependent methylation writers, including DNA methyltransferases, histone methyltransferases, and the METTL3/METTL14/WTAP m6A writer complex. In parallel, DNA, histone, and m6A demethylation are regulated by metabolically sensitive erasers. TET enzymes, Jumonji C-domain histone demethylases, FTO, and ALKBH5 require α-ketoglutarate (α-KG), O 2 , and Fe 2+ , whereas LSD1/KDM1A uses flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD)-dependent oxidative chemistry; succinate and fumarate can inhibit α-KG-dependent demethylation. The balance between methylation writing and erasing shapes context-dependent net methylation states that contribute to the adaptive methylation landscape. These states influence transcriptional and post-transcriptional reprogramming and thereby contribute to epithelial–mesenchymal plasticity (EMP), including epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT), cancer stemness, tumor dormancy, drug-tolerant persister (DTP) states, lineage plasticity, immune evasion, and therapy resistance.

papers.title: A dual-function XCL1-CD40L mRNA adjuvant potentiates cancer vaccines by coordinating DC recruitment and maturation.
papers.authors: Wu C, Shao W, Liu Y, Pan S, Wang W, Deng L, Zhang S, Cui Z, Wang Y, He P, Yang Y, Zhao Y.
papers.abstract: Background Despite the significant promise of mRNA tumor vaccines in treating solid tumors, their clinical response rate is constrained by the low effectiveness of antigen presentation resulting from the immune-suppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1) are pivotal in antigen cross-presentation; yet, they frequently exhibit insufficient immune-activating communication within solid malignancies. Methods This investigation comprehensively examined the functional attributes of cDC1 by TCGA cohorts and single-cell transcriptomic data. Guided by these bioinformatic insights, we engineered and synthesized a dual-functional mRNA adjuvant encoding the mXCL1-mCD40L fusion protein. We assessed the biological functions and anti-tumor efficacy of this adjuvant in combination with Glypican-3 (GPC3) and HPV-associated mRNA vaccines via protein expression, structure prediction, in vivo antigen uptake and presentation assays, antigen-presenting cell activation assays, antigen-specific T cell activation tests, and therapeutic studies in tumor-bearing mouse models. Results A high cDC1 signature score was associated with improved overall survival across LIHC and SKCM TCGA cohorts. Compared to normal sample, cDC1s in HCC and melanoma retained their antigen-presentation machinery but received reduced activating ligand inputs (XCL1-XCR1 signaling in HCC and CD40-CD40L signaling in melanoma). AlphaFold 3 showed that the mXCL1-mCD40L fusion protein can maintain structural integrity without spatial steric hindrance. The fusion protein was confirmed to be secreted and to retain both XCL1-dependent chemotactic activity and CD40-dependent dendritic-cell activation. mXCL1-mCD40L mRNA-LNP activated macrophages and dendritic cells in vitro , upregulating immune-related gene expression as confirmed by qPCR. In vivo , the dual-functional adjuvant significantly enhanced the anti-tumor effect of the GPC3 vaccine, outperformed co-delivery of separate mXCL1 and mCD40L mRNA-LNP, and induced stronger specific IFN-γ producing T cells. Meanwhile, this adjuvant also boosted the anti-tumor efficacy of HPV-associated mRNA vaccines. Mechanistically, this adjuvant increased tumor-antigen acquisition and cross-presentation by CD103 + DCs and promoted DC maturation in draining lymph nodes, accompanied by an increased proportion of peripheral CD8 + T cells. Conclusion By enhancing the recruitment and maturation of cDC1s, the dual-function mXCL1-mCD40L mRNA adjuvant boosts the efficacy of GPC3 and HPV-associated mRNA vaccines, supporting its potential as an antigen-flexible adjuvant platform against solid tumors.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and functional analyses identify LAIR1 as a key immunoregulatory molecule in postoperative sepsis.
papers.authors: Liu T, Wang Y, Zeng L, Miao X, Peng Y, Yu J, Li J, Zhao Q, Chen Z, Dai R, Li H.
papers.abstract: Background Postoperative sepsis arises from a dysregulated host response to infection following surgical stress. Current non-specific biomarkers offer insufficient predictive value, highlighting the need to identify molecular signatures that may facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative sepsis while providing insight into the underlying immune regulatory mechanisms. Methods Transcriptomic datasets comprising postoperative septic and non-septic surgical cohorts, together with independent cohorts of sepsis and non-infectious systemic inflammation, were analyzed using Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis and machine-learning approaches to identify hub genes. A diagnostic nomogram was constructed and validated across independent cohorts. A murine postoperative endotoxemia model (tibial fracture surgery followed by LPS challenge) was used for in vivo validation. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis and LAIR1 antibody blockade were performed to assess cellular and functional relevance. Results A four-gene signature comprising LAIR1, PLAC8, ACSS2, and PCOLCE2 was identified. The resulting model achieved AUCs of 0.865 in GSE131761, 0.965 in GSE74224, 0.827 in E-MTAB-1548, 0.929 in GSE65682, and 0.997 in GSE77167. Among the four genes, LAIR1 showed the most sustained upregulation in peripheral blood and multiple organs during postoperative endotoxemia. Single-cell analysis identified monocytes as the predominant circulating source of LAIR1. LAIR1 blockade increased systemic cytokine release, aggravated multiorgan injury, and reduced survival. Conclusions The four-gene signature reproducibly distinguished sepsis from infection-negative systemic inflammation across surgical and broader ICU cohorts. LAIR1 exhibited monocyte-enriched expression and a protective immunoregulatory role in postoperative endotoxemia, supporting its relevance to immune dysregulation of sepsis.
